\subsection{Discussion}

In our setting, the diagrams for properties $\alpha$ and $\gamma$ 
in Figure \ref{FigHuetConfluencePropertiesAlphaBetaGamma} are important because
they have (local) peaks involving $\genrelation$ and $\genequivalence$ only.
%
This is important in practice: as shown in \cite[Section 3.4]{Huet_ConfReduc_JACM80}, in the realm of (equational) term rewriting systems $\cR=(\Symbols,E,R)$, properties $\alpha$ and $\gamma$ can be ensured as the joinability (modulo) 
of \emph{ordinary} critical pairs $\langle s,t\rangle$ \cite[page 809]{Huet_ConfReduc_JACM80}
obtained from \emph{both}
the rules in $R$ and also from the rules obtained by orienting the equations $\elhsr\equequ{}\erhsr$ 
in $E$ as rules $\elhsr\to\erhsr$ and $\erhsr\to\elhsr$ \cite[Lemmata 3.4 and 3.5]{Huet_ConfReduc_JACM80}.
Furthermore, joinability of critical pairs $\langle s,t\rangle$ is tested as $s\rews{\cR}\circ\equequ{E}\circ\leftrews{\cR}t$ (usually called \emph{joinability modulo}, written $\ejoinability{}$ in \cite{Huet_ConfReduc_JACM80}).

\medskip
In sharp contrast (see Figure \ref{FigConfluenceAndCoherenceProperties}), 
(local) peaks in 
local confluence modulo $\genequivalence$ of $\genrelationUpE$ with $\genrelation$ 
and local coherence modulo $\genequivalence$ of $\genrelationUpE$ (local)  peaks involve 
$\genequivalence$, $\genrelation$, and \emph{also} $\genrelationUpE$. 
As a consequence,  if 
$\genequivalence$ is $\equequ{E}$, 
$\genrelation$ is $\rew{\cR}$, and
$\genrelationUpE$ is the Peterson and Stickel's relation $\rew{\cR,E}$,
the analysis of the local properties requires
$E$-critical pairs.
%
$E$-critical pairs $\langle s,t\rangle$ \cite[Definition 12]{JouKir_CompletionOfASetOfRulesModuloASetOfEquations_SIAMJC86}
have a number of problems, as mentioned in the introduction (there can be infinitely many; they require $E$-unification algorithms which may \emph{fail} to exist,\ldots).
%
Also note that 
\begin{enumerate}
\item ordinary critical pairs are also $E$-critical pairs but not vice versa, i.e., the use of $E$-critical pairs amouts at having more pairs to test.
On the other hand,
\item  joinability of $E$-critical pairs 
$\langle s,t\rangle$ is tested as $s\rews{\cR,E}\circ\equequ{E}\circ\leftrews{\cR,E}t$, which is more \emph{powerful} than joinability modulo, as $\rews{\cR}\spcrel{\subseteq}\rews{\cR,E}$.
\end{enumerate}
%
Thus, after presenting \egtrs{s} in the next section, in
Section \ref{SecReductionAndCoherencePeaks} we  
make explicit the kind of peaks and joinability conditions 
we need to consider to 
prove and disprove confluence modulo of \egtrs{s}
in the remainder of the paper.

\section{Equational Generalized Term Rewriting Systems}
\label{SecEGTRSs}

The following definition introduces the kind of computational systems we consider here which can be viewed as an specialization of \emph{Generalized Term Rewriting Systems} (\gtrs{s}) introduced in \cite{Lucas_LocalConferenceOfConditionalAndGeneralizedTermRewritingSystems_JLAMP24}
(see Section \ref{SecRelatedWork} for a more detailed comparison).
%
\begin{definition}[Equational Generalized Term Rewriting Systems]
\label{DefCS_ECTRS}
An \emph{Equational Generalized Term Rewriting System (\egtrs{})} is a tuple
$\cR=(\Symbols,\SPredicates,\mu,E,H,R)$ where 
$\Symbols$ is a signature of function symbols
$\SPredicates$ is a signature of predicate symbols with $\ceq,\rew{},\rews{}\in\SPredicates$,
$\mu$ is a replacement map for the signature $\Symbols$ of function symbols,
and,
\begin{itemize}
\item $E$ is a set of conditional equations $s\ceq t\IF \gencond$, for terms $s$ and $t$;
\item $H$ is a set of definite Horn clauses $A\IF \gencond$ where $A=P(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$ for some terms $t_1,\ldots,t_n$, $n\geq 0$, is such that $P\notin\{\ceq,\rew{},\rews{}\}$; and 
\item $R$ is a set of conditional rules $\lhsr\to\rhsr\IF\gencond$ for terms $\lhsr\notin\Variables$ and $\rhsr$.
\end{itemize}
%
where $\gencond$ is a sequence of atomic formulas.
\end{definition}
%
Note that $E\cup H\cup R$ is a set of (definite) Horn clauses.
Requiring $\rootTerm(A)\notin\{\ceq,\rew{},\rews{}\}$ for all $A\IF \gencond\in H$ ensures that 
computational predicates $\ceq$, $\rew{}$, and $\rews{}$ 
are defined by $E$ and $R$ only (with an \emph{auxiliary} use of $H$). 
%
\begin{example}
\label{ExSumListsA_EGTRS}
The \egtrs{} 
in Example \ref{ExSumListsA} is

\begin{remark}[Conditions $s\cto t$ and their interpretation]
\label{RemInterpretationOfCto}
In the literature about \emph{Conditional TRSs}
(CTRSs, see, e.g., \cite[Chapter 7]{Ohlebusch_AdvTopicsTermRew_2002}), 
symbol $\cto$ is often used to 
specify conditions 
$s\cto t$ in rules having different \emph{interpretations}: as \emph{joinability}, \emph{reachability}, 
etc.\ \cite[Definition 7.1.3]{Ohlebusch_AdvTopicsTermRew_2002}.
%
In \egtrs{s}, $\cto$ would be treated as a predicate in $\SPredicates$ and
the desired interpretation is \emph{explicitly} 
obtained by including in $H$ an appropriate set 
of clauses defining $\cto$.
%
For instance, 
(\ref{ExSumListsA_clause3}) in Example \ref{ExSumListsA} interprets $\cto$ as \emph{reachability}.
\end{remark}

\begin{notation}
 Equations $s\ceq t\IF\gencond$ in $E$ are often \emph{transformed} 
into rules 
by chosing a \emph{left-to-right} or \emph{right-to-left} orientation:
\[\overrightarrow{E}=\{s\to t\IF\gencond\mid s\ceq t\IF\gencond\in E\} \text{ and }
\overleftarrow{E}=\{t\to s\IF\gencond\mid s\ceq t\IF\gencond\in E\}.\]
%
We let $\eqoriented{E}=\overrightarrow{E}\cup\overleftarrow{E}$.
%
Note that $\eqoriented{E}$ may contain rules $\elhsr\to\erhsr\IF\gencond$ whose left-hand side
$\elhsr$ is a \emph{variable}.
Let $\DSymbols(\eqoriented{E})=\{\rootTree(\elhsr)\in\Symbols\mid \elhsr\to\erhsr\IF\gencondbis\in\eqoriented{E}\}$.
\end{notation}
%
\begin{definition}
We say that $P\in\SPredicates$  \emph{depends on $R$} 
if $P\in\{\rew{},\rews{}\}$ 
or there is $A\IF A_1,\ldots,A_n\in E\cup H$ with $\rootTerm(A)=P$
such that $\rootTerm(A_i)$ depends on $R$ for some $1\leq i\leq n$.
\end{definition}
%
\subsection{First-order theory of an \egtrs{}}
\label{SecFirstOrderTheoryOfAnEGRS}
%
In this paper, \emph{computational relations} (e.g., $\equequ{E}$, 
$\rew{\cR}$, $\rew{\cR,E}$, $\rew{\cR/E}$,\ldots) 
induced by an \egtrs{} $\cR=(\Symbols,\SPredicates,\mu,E,H,R)$
are defined by deduction of atoms 
$s = t$ (equality in $E$),
$s\to t$ (one-step rewriting in the usual sense), 
$s\rewpstickel{}t$ (rewriting modulo \`a la Peterson \& Stickel), 
$s\rewmodulo{}t$ (rewriting modulo), 
etc., in
some FO-theory. 
%
We \emph{extend} 
$\SPredicates$ with 
$\rewpstickel{}$, $\rewmodulo{}$, etc., and also
$\cto_\PSabbr$, $\cto_\RMabbr$ (as they depend on the previous predicates).
Our FO-theories are obtained from the generic sentences in Table \ref{TableFOSentencesEGRSs},
%
\begin{table}
\caption{Generic sentences of the FO-theory of \egtrs{s}}
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{l@{~}l}
Label & Sentence\\
\hline
$(\RuleReflexivity)^\gbop$ 
&
$(\forall x)~x \mathrel{\gbop} x$
\\
$(\RuleTransitivity)^\gbop$ 
& $(\forall x,y,z)~x \:\gbop\: y\wedge y \:\gbop\: z\Rightarrow x  
\:\gbop\: z$ 
\\
$(\RuleSymmetry)^\gbop$ 
& $(\forall x,y)~y\:\gbop\:x\Rightarrow x \:\gbop\: y$
\\
$(\RuleCompatibility)^\gbop$ 
& 
$(\forall x,y,z)~x \:\gbop\: y\wedge y
  \:\gbop^*\: z\Rightarrow x  
\:\gbop^*\: z$
\\
$(\RulePropagation)^\gbop_{f,i}$
& 
$(\forall x_1,\ldots,x_k,y_i)~x_i\:\gbop\: y_i\Rightarrow f(x_1,\ldots,x_i,\ldots,x_k)\:\gbop\: f(x_1,\ldots,y_i,\ldots,x_k)$
\\
$(\RuleHornClause)_{A\IF A_1,\ldots,A_n}$ 
& $(\forall\vec{x})~A_1\wedge\cdots\wedge A_n\Rightarrow A$ 
\\
$(\RuleRlEq)_{\lhsr\to \rhsr\IF A_1,\ldots,A_n}$
& $(\forall x,\vec{x})~x = \lhsr\wedge A_1\wedge\cdots\wedge A_n\Rightarrow x \rpstickel \rhsr$
\\
$(\RuleRewMEq)$ 
& $(\forall x,x',y,y')~x = x'\wedge x'\to y' \wedge y'= y\Rightarrow x \rmodulo{} y$  
\\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
\label{TableFOSentencesEGRSs}
\end{table}
%
where:
\begin{itemize}
\item Sentences $(\RuleReflexivity)^\gbop$, 
$(\RuleTransitivity)^\gbop$, and 
$(\RuleSymmetry)^\gbop$, which are parametric on a binary relation $\gbop$, 
 express \emph{reflexivity}, \emph{transitivity}, and \emph{symmetry} of  $\gbop$, respectively;
\item $(\RuleCompatibility)^\gbop$ expresses \emph{compatibility} of one-step 
and many-step reduction with $\gbop$;
\item for each $k$-ary function symbol $f$, $1\leq i\leq k$, and $x_1,\ldots,x_k$ and $y_i$ distinct variables,
$(\RulePropagation)^\gbop_{f,i}$ \emph{propagates} an $\gbop$-step to the $i$-th immediate subterm of an $f$-rooted term;
\item $(\RuleHornClause)_\alpha$ presents a clause $\alpha:A\IF A_1,\ldots,A_n$, 
with variables $\vec{x}$ as a sentence.
\item $(\RuleRlEq)_{\alpha}$
defines a Peterson \& Stickel rewriting step $s\rew{\cR,E}t$ (at the root) using rule $\alpha:\lhsr\to\rhsr\IF\gencond$ with variables $\vec{x}$. Here, $x\notin\vec{x}$.
\item $(\RuleRewMEq)$ defines reduction modulo $\rew{\cR/E}$ in the usual way.
\end{itemize}
%
The following example illustrates the differences between 
(i) rewriting with $\rew{\cR}$ (where a term $t$ is rewritten if 
$t|_p=\sigma(\lhsr)$ for some position $p$ in $t$, 
rule $\lhsr\to\rhsr\IF\gencond$ in $\cR$,
and substitution $\sigma$ such that $\sigma(\gencond)$ holds), 
(ii) rewriting modulo $\rew{\cR/E}$ (where a term $t$ is rewritten if it is $E$-equivalent to
another term $t'$ to which a rewrite rule applies as above), 
and 
(iii) rewriting \emph{\`a la Peterson \& Stickel} $\rew{\cR,E}$
(where a term $t$ is rewritten if some subterm $t|_p$ is $E$-equivalent to
an instance $\sigma(\lhsr)$ of the left-hand side $\lhsr$ of a rewrite rule $\lhsr\to\rhsr\IF\gencond$ and $\sigma(\gencond)$ holds).
%
\begin{example}
\label{ExPeakNoCPs}
\label{ExPeakNoCPs_ETRS}
Consider  
$E=\{(\ref{ExPeakNoCPs_eq1}),(\ref{ExPeakNoCPs_eq2})\}$
and 
$\cR=(\Symbols,R)$ with $R=\{(\ref{ExPeakNoCPs_rule1}),
(\ref{ExPeakNoCPs_rule2})\}$, where
%
\begin{eqnarray}
\fS{b} & =  & \fS{f}(\fS{a})\label{ExPeakNoCPs_eq1}\\
\fS{a} & =  & \fS{c}\label{ExPeakNoCPs_eq2}\\
\fS{c} & \to & \fS{d}\label{ExPeakNoCPs_rule1}\\
\fS{b} & \to & \fS{d}\label{ExPeakNoCPs_rule2}
\end{eqnarray}
%
Then, 
\begin{itemize}
\item $\fS{f}(\fS{a})$ is $\rew{\cR}$-irreducible. However, 
$\fS{f}(\fS{a})\rew{\cR,E}\fS{f}(\fS{d})$ 
because 
$\fS{a}\equequ{E}\ul{\fS{c}}\rew{\cR}\fS{d}$.
%
However, 
\item $\fS{b}\rew{\cR/E}\fS{f}(\fS{d})$ because $\fS{b}\equequ{E}\fS{f}(\fS{a})\equequ{E}\fS{f}(\ul{\fS{c}})\rew{\cR}\fS{f}(\fS{d})$, but $\fS{b}\not\rew{\cR,E}\fS{f}(\fS{d})$.
\end{itemize}
\end{example}
%
Now, consider the following \emph{parametric} theories with parameters
$\SigParameter$ (referring to a signature),
$\RMaParameter$ (a replacement map),
$\EqParameter$ (a set of equations), and
$\TRSParameter$ (a set of rules):

\vspace{-0.2cm}
{\footnotesize
\[\begin{array}{rcl}
\GLtheory_{\text{Eq}}[\SigParameter,\RMaParameter,\EqParameter] 
& = &
\{(\RuleReflexivity)^{\equequ{}},
(\RuleSymmetry)^{\equequ{}},
(\RuleTransitivity)^=\}
\}
\cup\{(\RulePropagation)^{\equequ{}}_{f,i}\mid f\in\SigParameter,i\in\RMaParameter(f)\}\cup\{(\RuleHornClause)_e\mid e\in\EqParameter\}
\\
%
\GLtheory_{\text{R}}[\SigParameter,\RMaParameter,\TRSParameter] 
& = & \{
(\RuleReflexivity)^{\to^*},
(\RuleCompatibility)^{\to}\}
\cup
\{(\RulePropagation)^\to_{f,i}\mid f\in \SigParameter,i\in\RMaParameter(f)\}\cup\{(\RuleHornClause)_\alpha\mid\alpha\in \TRSParameter\}
\}
\\  
\GLtheory_{\text{R,M}}[\SigParameter,\RMaParameter,\TRSParameter]
& = & 
\{
(\RuleReflexivity)^{\rewspstickel{}},
(\RuleCompatibility)^{\rewpstickel{}}\}
\cup
\{(\RulePropagation)^{\rewpstickel{}}_{f,i}\mid f\in \SigParameter,i\in\RMaParameter(f)\}\cup\{(\RuleRlEq)_\alpha\mid\alpha\in \TRSParameter\}
\\  
\GLtheory_{\text{R/M}}[\SigParameter,\RMaParameter,\TRSParameter]
& = & \{
(\RuleReflexivity)^{\rmStar},
(\RuleCompatibility)^{\rmodulo}
\}
\cup
\{(\RulePropagation)^{\to}_{f,i}\mid f\in \SigParameter,i\in\RMaParameter(f))\}\cup\{(\RuleHornClause)_\alpha\mid\alpha\in \TRSParameter\}
\}
\cup
\{
(\RuleRewMEq)
\}
\end{array}
\]
}
%
Note that, in $\GLtheory_{\text{R/M}}[\SigParameter,\RMaParameter,\TRSParameter]$ 
propagation sentences are given for $\rew{}$ rather than for $\rmodulo$;
this is consistent with the usual definition of rewriting modulo implemented by 
(\RuleRewMEq).

Since rules $\alpha:\lhsr\to\rhsr\IF\gencond$ in $R$ 
are used to specify 
\emph{different} computational relations (see Definition \ref{DefComputationalRelationsOfAnEGTRS}), 
conditions $s\cto t\in\gencond$
have different \emph{interpretations} depending on the targetted relation:
%
the meaning of $\cto$ is based on predicate $\rew{}$ if $\alpha$ is
used to describe the usual (conditional) rewrite relation $\rew{\cR}$;
%
however, 
$\cto$ should be treated using $\rpstickel$ if $\alpha$ is used to describe Peterson \& Stickel's rewriting modulo $\rew{\cR,E}$;
and
$\cto$ should be treated using $\rmodulo$ if $\alpha$ is used to describe %rewriting modulo 
$\rew{\cR/E}$.
%
A simple way to deal with this situation is the following.

\begin{definition}
Let $\cR=(\Symbols,\SPredicates,\mu,E,H,R)$ be an \egtrs{}.
\begin{itemize}
\item $H^\PSabbr$ (resp.\ $H^\RMabbr$) is obtained from $H$ by replacing 
in each $A\IF A_1,\ldots,A_n\in H$ all occurrences of
$\cto$, $\rew{}$ and 
$\rews{}$ by $\cto_\PSabbr$, $\rewpstickel{}$ and $\rewspstickel{}$ (resp.\ $\cto_\RMabbr$, $\rewmodulo{}$, and $\rewmodulos{\!\!}$).
\item $R^\PSabbr$ ($R^\RMabbr$) is obtained from $R$ by replacing 
all occurrences of
$\cto$ in each $\lhsr\to\rhsr\IF\gencond\in R$  by $\cto_\PSabbr$ ($\cto_\RMabbr$).
\end{itemize}
\end{definition}
%
%
\begin{remark}[Predicate $\equequ{}$ does not depend on $R$]
\label{RemEqDoesNotDependOnR}
In the following, we will assume that $\equequ{}$ does \emph{not} 
depend on $R$. Thus, 
the ``meaning'' of equational atoms $s\equequ{} t$ does \emph{not} depend on the \emph{rules} in 
$R$.
%
For this reason, we do not need versions $\equequ{ps}$ or $\equequ{rm}$
of the equality predicate.
%
Similarly, $E^\PSabbr$ or $E^\RMabbr$ are not necessary.
\end{remark}
%

R^\RMabbr=\{(\ref{ExSumListsA_rule1_RM}),(\ref{ExSumListsA_rule2_RM}),(\ref{ExSumListsA_rule3_RM}),(\ref{ExSumListsA_rule4_RM})\}\] with:

x\cto_\RMabbr y & \IF & x\rewmodulos{}y\label{ExSumListsA_clause3_RM}
\\

 \fS{Nat}(m), \fS{sum}(\cfrozen{ns})\cto_\RMabbr n\label{ExSumListsA_rule4_RM}

 \end{example}

\begin{remark}[Proving infeasibility as satisfiability]
As explained in \cite[Section 4.3]{GutLuc_AutomaticallyProvingAndDisprovingFeasibilityConditions_IJCAR20}, the infeasibility of an atom $\GLatom$ with variables $\vec{x}$
with respect to a first-order theory $\GLtheory$  (i.e., the absence of a substitution $\sigma$ such that $\deductionInThOf{\GLtheory}{\sigma(\GLatom)}$ holds),
can be 
proved by finding a model $\SInterpretation$ 
of $\GLtheory\cup\neg(\exists\vec{x})\GLatom$.
%
Such first-order odels can often 
be automatically obtained by using model generators like 
\AGES{} \cite{GutLuc_AutomaticGenerationOfLogicalModelsWithAGES_CADE19} or \MaceFour{} \cite{McCune_Prove9andMace4_Unpublished10}.
%
\end{remark}

In Example \ref{ExPeakNoCPs} we claim that $\fS{b}$ does not reduce into $\fS{f}(\fS{d})$ in one step of $\rew{\cR,E}$.
%
The following interpretation $\SInterpretation$ over the positive integers (computed by \AGES), with 
%
\[\begin{array}{r@{~}c@{~}l@{\hspace{1cm}}r@{~}c@{~}l@{\hspace{1cm}}r@{~}c@{~}l@{\hspace{1cm}}r@{~}c@{~}l}
\fS{a}^\SInterpretation & = & 1
& 
\fS{b}^\SInterpretation & = & 1
&
\fS{b}^\SInterpretation & = & 1
&
\fS{b}^\SInterpretation & = & 1
\\
\fS{f}^\SInterpretation(x) & = & 2
&
x\equequ{}^\SInterpretation y & \Leftrightarrow& true
&
x(\rewpstickel{})^\SInterpretation y & \Leftrightarrow & x\geq_\naturals y
&
x(\rewspstickel{})^\SInterpretation y & \Leftrightarrow & true
\end{array}
\]
%
satisfies 
$\GLtheory_{\cR,E}\cup\{\neg\fS{b}\rewpstickel{}\fS{f}(\fS{d})\}$, 
thus formally proving our claim.

%
When necessary, \AGES{} and \MaceFour{} are often useful to prove infeasibility of rules, conditional pairs, joinability of terms, etc., see \cite[Figures 4--6]{Lucas_ProvingSemanticPropertiesAsFirstOrderSatisfiability_AI19} for some examples of use of first-order satisfiability when dealing with rewriting-based systems.

\subsection{Computation with \egtrs{s}. Confluence and termination modulo}

The theories above are used to define the expected computational relations as follows.

\begin{definition}
\label{DefComputationalRelationsOfAnEGTRS}
Let $\cR=(\Symbols,\SPredicates,\mu,E,\mu,H,R)$ be an \egtrs{} and $s,t\in\Terms$.
\begin{itemize}
\item 
We write 
$s\equequ{E}t$  
(resp.\ $s\rew{\eqoriented{E}}t$) 
iff 
$\deductionInThOf{\GLtheory_{E}}{s\equequ{}t}$ 
(resp.\ $\deductionInThOf{\GLtheory_{R}[\Symbols,\mu,\eqoriented{E}]}{s\rew{}t}$)
holds.
%
\item 
We write $s\rew{\cR}t$ (resp.\ $s\rew{\cR,E}t$ and $s\rew{\cR/E}t$) iff
$\deductionInThOf{\GLtheory_{\cR}}{s\rew{}t}$
(resp.\ $\deductionInThOf{\GLtheory_{\cR,E}}{s\rewpstickel{}t}$ and
$\deductionInThOf{\GLtheory_{\cR/E}}{s\rewmodulo{}t}$) holds.
%
Similarly for $s\rews{\cR}t$ (resp.\ $s\rews{\cR,E}t$ and $s\rews{\cR/E}t$).
\end{itemize}
\end{definition}
%
Note that 
(i) $\rew{\eqoriented{E}}$ is \emph{symmetric} by definition of $\eqoriented{E}$;
%
(ii) $\equequ{E}$ is an equivalence due to 
$(\RuleReflexivity)^{\equequ{}}$ (reflexivity),
$(\RuleSymmetry)^{\equequ{}}$ (symmetry), and
$(\RuleTransitivity)^{\equequ{}}$ (transitivity),
all 
included in $\GLtheory_{E}$; 
and
%
(iii) $\equequ{E}$ is the reflexive and transitive closure of $\rew{\eqoriented{E}}$.

\begin{definition}[Confluence and termination modulo of an \egtrs{}]
\label{DefConfluenceAndTerminationModuloOfEGTRSs}
Let $\cR=(\Symbols,\SPredicates,\mu,E,H,R)$ be an \egtrs{}. We say that 
\begin{itemize}
\item $\cR$ is \emph{confluent modulo $E$}
(or  \emph{$E$-confluent}) iff for all terms
$t$, $t_1$, and $t_2$, if 
$t\rews{\cR/E}t_1$ 
and
$t\rews{\cR/E}t_2$,
then  there are $t'_1$ and $t'_2$ such that
$t_1\rews{\cR/E}t'_1$,
%
$t_2\rews{\cR/E}t'_2$ 
and $t'_1\equequ{E} t'_2$.
\item $\cR$ is \emph{terminating modulo $E$} (or \emph{$E$-terminating}) iff
$\rew{\cR/E}$ is terminating.
\end{itemize}
\end{definition}
%
\begin{remark}[Necessary conditions for $E$-termination]
\label{RemANecessaryConditionForETermination}
Regarding \etrs{s} $\cR=(\Symbols,E,R)$, in 
\cite[page 1169]{JouKir_CompletionOfASetOfRulesModuloASetOfEquations_SIAMJC86},
Jouannaud and Kirchner noticed that:
\begin{itemize}
\item if $E$ contains 
equations $s=t$ such that $\Var(s)\neq\Var(t)$ (so that there is a variable $x$ occurring in $s$ but not occurring in $t$), 
then $E$-termination is not possible. Consider substitutions $\sigma$ and $\sigma'$ such that $\sigma(x)=\lhsr$ for some rule $\lhsr\to\rhsr\in R$, $\sigma'(x)=\rhsr$, and $\sigma(y)=\sigma'(y)=y$ for all $y\in\Variables-\{x\}$.
%
Then, it is possible to define an infinite $\rew{\cR/E}$-reduction sequence $t=\sigma(t)\equequ{E}\sigma(s)\rewp{\cR}\sigma'(s)\equequ{E}\sigma'(t)=t$.
%
For this reason, \emph{non-erasingness} is assumed for the equational component $E$ of an \etrs{}, i.e., for all $s\ceq t\in E$, $\Var(s)=\Var(t)$.\footnote{In the realm of unification theory, this condition was called \emph{regularity}
\cite[page 243]{Siekmann_UnificationTheory_JSC89}. The term is also used in recent papers investigating confluence modulo, e.g.,
\cite[Section 2]{DurMes_OnTheChurchRosserAndCoherencePropertiesOfConditionalOrderSortedRewriteTheories_JLAP12} and
\cite[Section 2.1]{Meseguer_StrictCoherenceOfConditionalRewritingModuloAxioms_TCS17}.
}
Actually, $\Var(s)=\Var(t)$ for all $s\ceq t\in E$ is also assumed in Huet's work \cite[page 816, bottom]{Huet_ConfReduc_JACM80}. Although the requirement is not justified, the first sentence of page 819, discussing techniques for proving $E$-termination, makes sense only if such a condition holds.
%
\item Equations of the form $x=t$ where $t$ contains at least two occurrences of $x$ are also incompatible with $E$-termination.
For instance, if $t=t[x,x]$, 
we have
$\lhsr\equequ{E}t[\lhsr,\lhsr]\rew{\cR}t[\rhsr,\lhsr]\equequ{E} t[\rhsr,t[\lhsr,\lhsr]]\rew{\cR}t[\rhsr,t[\rhsr,\lhsr]]\rew{\cR/E}\cdots$.
%
The requirement of \emph{linearity} of equations in $E$ (i.e., for all $s\ceq t\in E$, both $s$ and $t$ are linear terms) 
imposed by other authors, e.g., 
\cite[Section 2.1]{Meseguer_StrictCoherenceOfConditionalRewritingModuloAxioms_TCS17}, overcomes this difficulty.
\end{itemize}
\end{remark}

\subsection{$E$-termination of \egtrs{s}}
\label{SecETerminationOfEGTRSs}
%
According to \cite{LucGut_AutomaticSynthesisOfLogicalModelsForOrderSortedFirstOrderTheories_JAR18,Lucas_UsingWellFoundedRelationsForProvingOperationalTermination_JAR20}, the $E$-termination of \egtrs{s} $\cR$ can be proved by 
showing a first-order model $\SInterpretation$ of $\GLtheory_{\cR/E}$ 
where the interpretation $(\rmodulo)^\SInterpretation$ of 
predicate $\rmodulo$ denoting $\rew{\cR/\cE}$ is \emph{well-founded}.
Again, \AGES{} or \MaceFour{} can be used to obtain 
such first-order models.
%
As explained in \cite[page 293]{GutLuc_AutomaticGenerationOfLogicalModelsWithAGES_CADE19} it is possible to instruct \AGES{} to guarantee that the interpretation $P^\SInterpretation$ of 
a binary predicate $P$ is a \emph{well-founded} relation on the interpretation domain.
%
This is not possible with \MaceFour; however, as explained in \cite[Section 5.5.1]{Lucas_UsingWellFoundedRelationsForProvingOperationalTermination_JAR20}, it is possible to force the tool to do the same.
%
When necessary, we use \AGES{} to prove $E$-termination of the considered \egtrs{s}.

The following example shows an interpretation proving $E$-termination of $\cR$ in
Example \ref{ExHuet80_RemarkPage818_EGTRS} automatically obtained by \AGES.
 
\begin{example}
\label{ExHuet80_RemarkPage818_ETermination}
For $\cR$ in Example \ref{ExHuet80_RemarkPage818_EGTRS},
%
the interpretation $\SInterpretation$ over the naturals, with 
\[\begin{array}{r@{~}c@{~}l@{\hspace{0.5cm}}r@{~}c@{~}l@{\hspace{0.5cm}}r@{~}c@{~}l@{\hspace{0.5cm}}r@{~}c@{~}l}
\fS{a}^\SInterpretation & = & 1
& 
\fS{b}^\SInterpretation & = & 1
&
\fS{f}^\SInterpretation(x,y) & = & x+2y+1
&
\fS{g}^\SInterpretation(x) & = & 3x
\\
x\equequ{}^\SInterpretation y & \Leftrightarrow& x=_\naturals y
&
x\rew{}^\SInterpretation y & \Leftrightarrow & x>_\naturals y
&
x(\rewmodulo){\!\!}^\SInterpretation y & \Leftrightarrow & x>_\naturals y
&
x(\rewsmodulo){\!}^\SInterpretation y & \Leftrightarrow & x\geq_\naturals y
\end{array}
\]
%
is a model of $\GLtheory_{\cR/E}$ in Example \ref{ExHuet80_RemarkPage818_TheoryRModulo}. 
Since $(\rmodulo)^\SInterpretation$ is well-founded, 
%
$\cR$ is $E$-terminating.
\end{example}

\subsection{Use of Jouannaud \& Kirchner's abstract framework with \egtrs{s}}

Unfortunately, the relationship between $\rew{\cR}$, $\equequ{E}$, and $\rew{\cR/E}$, 
is \emph{not} as required in the abstract framework presented in Section \ref{SecAbstractFrameworkJK86}.
%
In particular, $\rew{\cR/E}\:=\:(\composeRel{\equequ{E}}{\composeRel{\rew{\cR}}{\equequ{E}}})$ does \emph{not} hold.

\begin{example}
\label{ExRModuloAndRrelativeE}
Consider the following \egtrs{}
%
\begin{eqnarray}
\fS{a} & = & \fS{b}\label{ExRModuloAndRrelativeE_eq1}\\
\fS{a} & \to & \fS{c}\label{ExRModuloAndRrelativeE_rule1}\\
\fS{a} & \to & \fS{d}\IF \fS{b} \rews{} \fS{c}\label{ExRModuloAndRrelativeE_rule2}\\
\fS{c} & \to & \fS{d}\label{ExRModuloAndRrelativeE_rule3}
\end{eqnarray}
%
We have $\fS{a}\rew{\cR}\fS{c}$; but (\ref{ExRModuloAndRrelativeE_rule2}) is 
$\GLtheory_{\Symbols,\cR}$-infeasible, hence $\fS{a}\not\rew{\cR}\fS{d}$. 
%
However, $\fS{a}\rew{\cR/E}\fS{d}$, as $\fS{b}\equequ{E}\fS{a}\rew{\cR}\fS{c}$, i.e.,
$\fS{b}\rew{\cR/E}\fS{c}$ and (\ref{ExRModuloAndRrelativeE_rule2}) can be used. 
Thus,
\begin{eqnarray*}
\rew{\cR}  & = &  \{(\fS{a},\fS{c}),(\fS{c},\fS{d})\}
\\
{(\equequ{E}\circ\rew{\cR}\circ\equequ{E})} & = & \{(\fS{a},\fS{c}),(\fS{b},\fS{c}),(\fS{c},\fS{d})\}
\\
\rew{\cR/E} & = & \{(\fS{a},\fS{c}),(\fS{b},\fS{c}),(\fS{a},\fS{d}),(\fS{b},\fS{d}),(\fS{c},\fS{d})\}
\end{eqnarray*}
Therefore,
$\rew{\cR/E}\:\neq(\equequ{E}\circ\rew{\cR}\circ\equequ{E})$.
\end{example} 
%
\begin{remark}[Rewriting modulo and rewriting in conditional systems]
Example \ref{ExRModuloAndRrelativeE} shows a \emph{mismatch} between the definition of
$\rew{\cR/E}$ for an \egtrs{} $\cR$ (Definition \ref{DefComputationalRelationsOfAnEGTRS}) 
and the \emph{abstract} definition (\ref{LblReductionModuloFromReductionAndEquivalence}), usually understood for ETRSs.
For \egtrs{s} (and already for CTRSs), the connection 
$\rew{\cR/E}\:=\:(\equequ{E}\circ\rew{\cR}\circ\equequ{E})$ 
is \emph{lost}. 
This is because conditions in rules are treated using, e.g., 
$\rews{\cR}$ to obtain $\rew{\cR}$ (see, e.g., \cite[Definition 7.1.4]{Ohlebusch_AdvTopicsTermRew_2002}), whereas computations with $\rew{\cR/E}$ 
evaluate conditions using $\rews{\cR/E}$ instead, see, e.g., \cite[page 819]{DurMes_OnTheChurchRosserAndCoherencePropertiesOfConditionalOrderSortedRewriteTheories_JLAP12}.
\end{remark}
%
We overcome this problem as follows.
\begin{definition}[CR-theory of an \egtrs{}]
\label{DefCRtheoryOfAnEGTRS}
Let $\cR=(\Symbols,\SPredicates,\mu,E,H,R)$ be an \egtrs{}. The CR-theory of $\cR$ is
\[\begin{array}{r@{\:}c@{\:}l}
\crtheoryOf{\cR} & = &
\GLtheory_{\text{Eq}}[\Symbols,\mu,E]
\cup\GLtheory_{\text{R}}[\Symbols,\mu,R^\RMabbr]
\cup\GLtheory_{\text{R,M}}[\Symbols,\mu,R^\RMabbr]
\cup\GLtheory_{\text{R/M}}[\Symbols,\mu,R^\RMabbr]
\cup\:\{(\RuleHornClause)_\alpha\mid\alpha\in H^\RMabbr\}
\end{array}
\]
\end{definition}
%
Then, $\rew{\cR^\RMabbr}$ and $\rew{\cR^\RMabbr,E}$ (and also $\rews{\cR^\RMabbr}$ and $\rews{\cR^\RMabbr,E}$) are defined as follows:
\[\begin{array}{rcl@{\hspace{1cm}and\hspace{1cm}}rcl}
s \rew{\cR^\RMabbr}t & \Leftrightarrow & \deductionInThOf{\crtheoryOf{\cR}}{s\rew{}t}
& 
s \rew{\cR^\RMabbr,E}t & \Leftrightarrow & \deductionInThOf{\crtheoryOf{\cR}}{s\rewpstickel{}t}
\end{array}
\]
%
In contrast to $\rew{\cR}$ and $\rew{\cR,E}$, to obtain 
$\rew{\cR^\RMabbr}$ and $\rew{\cR^\RMabbr,E}$ conditions %$s\cto t$ 
in rules are evaluated using $\rew{\cR/E}$ (instead of $\rew{\cR}$ and $\rew{\cR,E}$).
%
Now, the requirements (\ref{LblReductionModuloFromReductionAndEquivalence}) and 
(\ref{LblFundamentalAssumptionJK86}) are fulfilled.

\begin{proposition}
\label{PropRewritingModuloEGRSsAsComposition}
\label{PropFundamentalAssumptionForEGRSs}
Let $\cR=(\Symbols,\SPredicates,\mu,E,H,R)$ be an \egtrs{}. 
Then, 
\[\rew{\cR/E}\:=\:(\composeRel{\equequ{E}}{\composeRel{\rew{\cR^\RMabbr}}{\equequ{E}}})
\text{\qquad and  \qquad}
\rew{\cR^\RMabbr}\:\subseteq\:\rew{\cR^\RMabbr,E}\:\subseteq\:\rew{\cR/E}.\]
\end{proposition}
%
\begin{proof}
As for the first claim, we have $s\rew{\cR/E}t$ iff $\deductionInThOf{\crtheoryOf{\cR}}{s\rewmodulo{}t}$ iff
(i) $\deductionInThOf{\crtheoryOf{\cR}}{s\equequ{} s'}$ holds for some term $s'$,
(ii) $\deductionInThOf{\crtheoryOf{\cR}}{s'\rew{} t'}$ holds for some term $t'$,
and 
(iii) $\deductionInThOf{\crtheoryOf{\cR}}{t'\equequ{} t}$ holds; 
then   $(\RuleRewMEq)$ applies to conclude  $s\rewmodulo{}t$.
%
Thus, we have $s\equequ{E}s'$, $s'\rew{\cR^\RMabbr}t'$, and $t'\equequ{E}t$, i.e.,
$s\composeRel{\equequ{E}}{\composeRel{\rew{\cR^\RMabbr}}{\equequ{E}}}t$.

As for the second claim, 
in order to prove the first inclusion, 
since $s\rew{\cR^\RMabbr}t$ iff $\deductionInThOf{\crtheoryOf{\cR}}{s\rew{} t}$, we have 
two possibilities:
(i) there is a rule $\alpha:\lhsr\to\rhsr\IF\gencond\in R^\RMabbr$
and a substitution $\sigma$ such that $\deductionInThOf{\crtheoryOf{\cR}}{\sigma(A)}$ holds for all $A\in \gencond$, and then $s=\sigma(\lhsr)$ and $t=\sigma(\rhsr)$ due to the use of 
$(\RuleHornClause)_\alpha\in\GLtheory_{\text{R}}[\Symbols,\mu,R^\RMabbr]\subseteq\crtheoryOf{\cR}$.
%
In this case, we can use 
$(\RuleRlEq)_\alpha\in\GLtheory_{\text{R,E}}[\Symbols,R^\RMabbr]\subseteq\crtheoryOf{\cR}$
by just letting $\sigma(x)=\sigma(\lhsr)$ for $x$ the
fresh variable in $(\RuleRlEq)_\alpha$ and using $(\RuleReflexivity)^=\in\GLtheory_{\text{Eq}}[\Symbols,E]\subseteq\crtheoryOf{\cR}$ to conclude $\sigma(x)\equequ{E}\sigma(\lhsr)$, as 
required to conclude $s\rewpstickel{\cR^\RMabbr,E}t$.
%
The second case is (ii) the use of 
$(\RulePropagation)^{\rew{}}_{f,i}\in\GLtheory_{\text{R}}[\Symbols,R^\RMabbr]\subseteq\crtheoryOf{\cR}$ for some $k$-ary
symbol $f\in\Symbols$ and $i\in\mu(f)$ 
such that $s=f(s_1,\ldots,s_i,\ldots,s_k)$ for some
terms $s_1,\ldots,s_k$, $t=f(s_1,\ldots,t_i,\ldots,s_k)$ for some term $s_i$ and 
$\deductionInThOf{\crtheoryOf{\cR}}{s_i\rew{}t_i}$ holds.
%
By an inductive argument, we can assume that
$\deductionInThOf{\crtheoryOf{\cR}}{s_i\rewpstickel{}t_i}$ holds.
%
Then, by using
$(\RulePropagation)^{\rewpstickel{}}_{f,i}\in\GLtheory_{\text{R,E}}[\Symbols,\mu,R^\RMabbr]\subseteq\crtheoryOf{\cR}$ we conclude
$\deductionInThOf{\crtheoryOf{\cR}}{s\rewpstickel{}t}$.

For the inclusion $\rew{\cR^\RMabbr,E}\spcrel{\subseteq}\rew{\cR/E}$, we proceed similarly. Since $s\rew{\cR^\RMabbr,E}t$ iff $\deductionInThOf{\crtheoryOf{\cR}}{s\rewpstickel{} t}$, we have 
two possibilities:
(i) $(\RuleRlEq)_\alpha$ is used, i.e., 
there is a rule $\alpha:\lhsr\to\rhsr\IF\gencond\in R^\RMabbr$
and a substitution $\sigma$ such that 
(i.1) $\deductionInThOf{\crtheoryOf{\cR}}{\sigma(x)=\sigma(\lhsr)}$ for $x$ the
fresh variable in $(\RuleRlEq)_\alpha$,
(i.2) $\deductionInThOf{\crtheoryOf{\cR}}{\sigma(A)}$ holds for all $A\in \gencond$, 
and then 
(i.3) $s=\sigma(x)\equequ{E}\sigma(\lhsr)$ and $t=\sigma(\rhsr)$ to conclude $s\rew{\cR^\RMabbr,E}t$.
%
By (i.2), we know that $\deductionInThOf{\crtheoryOf{\cR}}{\sigma(\lhsr)\rew{}\sigma(\rhsr)}$
by using $(\RuleHornClause)_\alpha$,
i.e., $\sigma(\lhsr)\rew{\cR^\RMabbr}\sigma(\rhsr)$ holds.
%
Thus, we have $s\equequ{E}\sigma(\lhsr)\rew{\cR^\RMabbr}\sigma(\rhsr)\equequ{E}t$ and,
 by the first (already proved) claim of this proposition, $s\rew{\cR/E}t$.
%
The second case is (ii) the use of 
$(\RulePropagation)^{\rewpstickel{}}_{f,i}\in\GLtheory_{\text{R}}[\Symbols,\mu,R^\RMabbr]\subseteq\crtheoryOf{\cR}$ for some $k$-ary
symbol $f\in\Symbols$ and $i\in\mu(f)$  
such that $s=f(s_1,\ldots,s_i,\ldots,s_k)$ for some
terms $s_1,\ldots,s_k$, $t=f(s_1,\ldots,t_i,\ldots,s_k)$ for some term $s_i$ and 
$\deductionInThOf{\crtheoryOf{\cR}}{s_i\rewpstickel{}t_i}$ holds.
%
By an inductive argument, we can assume that $s_i\rew{\cR/E}t_i$ and by using the first 
claim of the proposition, $s_i\equequ{E}s'_i\rew{\cR^\RMabbr}t'_i\equequ{E}t_i$ for some terms
$s'_i$ and $t'_i$.
%
By using $(\RulePropagation)^=_{f,i}\in\GLtheory_{\text{Eq}}[\Symbols,\mu,R^\RMabbr]\subseteq\crtheoryOf{\cR}$, we conclude 
$s=f(s_1,\ldots,s_i,\ldots,s_k)\equequ{E}f(s_1,\ldots,s'_i,\ldots,s_k)$
and
$f(s_1,\ldots,t'_i,\ldots,s_k)\equequ{E}f(s_1,\ldots,t_i,\ldots,s_k)=t$.
%
Now, by $(\RulePropagation)^{\rew{}}_{f,i}$, we have
$f(s_1,\ldots,s'_i,\ldots,s_k)\rew{\cR^\RMabbr}f(s_1,\ldots,t'_i,\ldots,s_k)$.
%
Thus, 
$s\equequ{E}f(s_1,\ldots,s'_i,\ldots,s_k)\rew{\cR^\RMabbr}f(s_1,\ldots,t'_i,\ldots,s_k)\equequ{E}t$, i.e., $s\rew{\cR/E}t$.
\end{proof}
%
\begin{remark}[Use of Jouannaud \& Kirchner's abstract framework]
By  the first statement in Proposition \ref{PropRewritingModuloEGRSsAsComposition},
$E$-confluence of \egtrs{s} (Definition \ref{DefConfluenceAndTerminationModuloOfEGTRSs}) and $E$-confluence of $\rew{\cR^\RMabbr}$ (as an abstract relation on terms,  
Definition \ref{DefConfluenceAndTerminationModulo}) \emph{coincide}.
%
This enables the use of the notions in Section \ref{SecBasicNotionsJK86} to
analyze $E$-confluence of \egtrs{s}.
\end{remark}
%
The results in Section \ref{SecAbstractFrameworkJK86}
apply to \egtrs{s} according to the correspondence in Table \ref{TableARSsAndEGTRSs}.
%

\begin{tabular}{rcccccc}
Abstract reduction: & $\equone{\genequivalence}$ & $\equ{\genequivalence}$ & $\rew{\genrelation}$ & $\rew{\genrelationUpE}$ &  $\rew{\genrelation/\genequivalence}$
\\[0.3cm]
Application to \egtrs{s:} & $\rew{\eqoriented{E}}$
& $=_E$ & $\rew{\cR^\RMabbr}$ & $\rew{\cR^\RMabbr,E}$ & $\rew{\cR/E}$
\end{tabular}

%
Note that Corollary \ref{CoroEConfluence_Huet80} (from Huet's results) is equivalent to Corollary \ref{CoroTheorem5_JK86} if $\genrelation=\genrelationUpE=\rew{\cR^\RMabbr}$.
%
Thus, as a consequence of 
Corollary \ref{CoroEConfluence_Huet80} we have the following
two sufficient conditions for $E$-confluence of $E$-terminating \egtrs{s}. 

\begin{corollary}
\label{CoroSufficientCriteriaForEConfluenceOfEGRSs}
Let $\cR=(\Symbols,\SPredicates,\mu,E,H,R)$ be an 
$E$-terminating \egtrs{}. Then, $\cR$ is $E$-confluent if one of the following conditions hold:
\begin{enumerate}
\item\label{CoroSufficientCriteriaForEConfluenceOfEGRSs_Huet} 
$\rew{\cR^\RMabbr}$ and $\equone{E}$ (i.e., $\rew{\eqoriented{E}}$) satisfy properties $\alpha$ and $\gamma$, or
%
\item\label{CoroSufficientCriteriaForEConfluenceOfEGRSs_JK86}
 $\rew{\cR^\RMabbr,E}$ is locally confluent modulo $E$ with $\rew{\cR^\RMabbr}$ and locally coherent modulo $E$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}
%
The following result is essential in the analysis of peaks in Sections \ref{SecAnalysisOfRandCpeaks} and \ref{SecAnalysisOfPSRandCpeaks}.

\begin{proposition}
\label{PropUseOfRulesAndPositionsInRewritingSteps_EGTRSs}
Let $\cR=(\Symbols,\SPredicates,\mu,E,H,R)$ be a \egtrs{} and $s,t\in\Terms$.
%
\begin{enumerate}
\item\label{PropUseOfRulesAndPositionsInRewritingSteps_EGTRSs_R}
 If $s\rew{\cR^\RMabbr} t$, then there is $p\in\Pos^\mu(s)$ and $\lhsr\to\rhsr\IF\gencond\in R^\RMabbr$ such that
(i) $s|_p=\sigma(\lhsr)$ for some substitution $\sigma$, 
(ii) for all $A\in\gencond$, $\crtheoryOf{\cR}\vdash\sigma(A)$ holds,
and 
(iii) $t=s[\sigma(\rhsr)]_p$.
\item\label{PropUseOfRulesAndPositionsInRewritingSteps_EGTRSs_PStickel}
 If $s\to_{\cR^\RMabbr,E} t$, then there is $p\in\Pos^\mu(s)$ and $\lhsr\to\rhsr\IF\gencond\in R^\RMabbr$ such that
(i) $s|_p\equequ{E}\sigma(\lhsr)$ for some substitution $\sigma$, 
(ii) for all $A\in\gencond$, $\crtheoryOf{\cR}\vdash\sigma(A)$ holds,
and 
(iii) $t=s[\sigma(\rhsr)]_p$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}


\begin{proof}
Since $s\rew{\cR^\RMabbr}t$ iff $\deductionInThOf{\crtheoryOf{\cR}}{s\rew{} t}$, we have 
two possibilities:
\begin{enumerate}
\item There is a clause $(\RuleHornClause)_\alpha$
for some rule $\alpha:\lhsr\to\rhsr\IF \gencond\in R^\RMabbr$ 
and a substitution $\sigma$ such that $\deductionInThOf{\crtheoryOf{\cR}}{\sigma(A)}$ holds
for all $A\in\gencond$, and then $s=\sigma(\lhsr)$ and $t=\sigma(\rhsr)$.
%
In this case, we just need to take $p=\toppos$ to obtain the desired conclusion.
%
\item There is a clause $(\RulePropagation)_{f,i}$ for some $f\in\Symbols$ and
$i\in\mu(f)$
so that 
(a) $s=f(s_1,\ldots,s_i,\ldots,s_k)$ for some terms $s_1,\ldots,s_k$, 
(b) $t=f(s_1,\ldots,t_i,\ldots,s_k)$,
and $\deductionInThOf{\crtheoryOf{\cR}}{s_i\rew{}t_i}$ holds.
%
By the induction hypothesis, $s_i\rew{\cR^\RMabbr} t_i$
holds and
there is $q\in\Pos^\mu(s_i)$, $\lhsr\to\rhsr\IF\gencond\in\cR$ and
substitution $\sigma$ such that
$s_i|_q=\sigma(\lhsr)$, $t_i=s_i[\sigma(\rhsr)]_q$, and each atom in $\sigma(\gencond)$ is deducible from $\crtheoryOf{\cR}$.
%
Since $s|_{i.q}=\sigma(\lhsr)$ and $t=s[\sigma(\rhsr)]_{i.q}$, the conclusion follows by letting
$p=i.q$, which belongs to $\Pos^\mu(s)$ by definition of $\Pos^\mu$.
\end{enumerate}
The case $s\rew{\cR^\RMabbr,E} t$ is similar.
\end{proof}

\begin{notation}
For the sake of readability, in the following, if no confusion arises 
we drop $\RMabbr$ from $R^\RMabbr$ and 
$\cR^\RMabbr$ 
in $\rew{\cR^\RMabbr}$ and $\rew{\cR^\RMabbr,E}$
(and associated peak and joinability notions $\peak{\cR^\RMabbr}$, 
\ldots, $\joinability{\cR^\RMabbr}$, $\joinability{\cR^\RMabbr,E}$, etc.)
and write $\rew{\cR}$, $\rew{\cR,E}$, $\peak{\cR}$, 
\ldots,  $\joinability{\cR}$, $\joinability{\cR,E}$, etc.,
by assuming that the corresponding reduction relations are obtained as indicated in the paragraph below Definition \ref{DefCRtheoryOfAnEGTRS}. 
\end{notation}
%
\renewcommand{\RMabbr}{{}}
%
Also,if no confusion arises,  in the following we use \emph{(in)feasible} instead of 
\emph{$\crtheoryOf{\cR}$-(in)feasible}, i.e., theory $\crtheoryOf{\cR}$ is used for any statement about (in)feasibility of sequences of atoms.

\section{Reduction and coherence peaks}
\label{SecReductionAndCoherencePeaks}

According to Corollary \ref{CoroSufficientCriteriaForEConfluenceOfEGRSs},
in order to prove $E$-confluence of ($E$-terminating) \egtrs{s} $\cR$, we have to investigate 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\ejoin{\cR^\RMabbr}$-joinability of 
$\peak{\cR^\RMabbr}$-peaks (Property $\alpha$) 
and 
$\peakOf{\rew{\cR^\RMabbr}}{\equone{E}}$-peaks 
(Property $\gamma$), which we denote $\peakOf{\cR^\RMabbr}{E}$ for short and for the sake of readability; or
%
\item $\ejoin{\cR^\RMabbr,E}$-joinability of $\peakOf{\cR^\RMabbr,E}{\cR^\RMabbr}$-peaks (local confluence of $\rew{\cR^\RMabbr}$  modulo $E$ with $\cR^\RMabbr$)
and
$\ejoinability{\cR^\RMabbr,E}$-joinability of 
$\peakOf{\cR^\RMabbr,E}{E}$-peaks (local coherence of $\rew{\cR^\RMabbr}$  modulo $E$).
\end{enumerate}
%
Roughly speaking, we need to consider two families of peaks as described in the following.

\section{Conditional pairs for proving $E$-confluence of \egtrs{s}}
\label{SecConditionalPairs}

In Sections \ref{SecAnalysisOfRandCpeaks} and \ref{SecAnalysisOfPSRandCpeaks}, we investigate how 
(PS-) r-peaks 
and c-peaks
of \emph{terms} can be proved (or disproved to be) joinable. 
%
For this purpose, we use \emph{general conditional pairs}, or just
\emph{conditional pairs}, 
as in \cite[Section 5]{Lucas_LocalConferenceOfConditionalAndGeneralizedTermRewritingSystems_JLAMP24}:
%
\begin{definition}[Conditional pair]
\label{DefConditionalPair}
A \emph{conditional pair} 
is an expression
\begin{eqnarray}
\underbrace{\langle s,t\rangle}_{\text{peak}} \IF  \underbrace{A_1,\ldots,A_n}_{\text{conditional part}}
\label{LblConditionalPair}
\end{eqnarray}
%
where $s$ and $t$ are terms and $A_1,\ldots,A_n$ are atoms.
\end{definition}
%
A conditional pair (\ref{LblConditionalPair}) is \emph{trivial} if $s=t$.
%
Conditional pairs $\langle s,t\rangle\IF\gencond$ and $\langle t,s\rangle\IF\gencond$, whose peaks are symmetric but share the same conditional part (possibly after reordering the atoms) are called \emph{symmetric}.
%
\begin{definition}[Joinability of conditional pairs]
\label{DefJoinabilityOfConditionalPairs}
Let $\cR$ 
be an \egtrs{}
and $\genrelation,\genrelationbis$ be relations on terms.
A conditional pair $\pi:\langle s,t\rangle\IF\gencond$ is 
$\joinOf{\genrelation}{\genrelationbis}$-joinable
if for all
substitutions $\sigma$, if 
$\deductionInThOf{\crtheoryOf{\cR}}{\sigma(A)}$
holds for all $A\in\gencond$, 
 then $\sigma(s)$ and $\sigma(t)$ are 
 $\joinOf{\genrelation}{\genrelationbis}$-joinable.
 \end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Feasible conditional pair]
\label{DefFeasibleConditionalPair}
Let $\cR$ be an \egtrs{}.
A general conditional pair 
$\langle s,t\rangle\IF\gencond$ is 
\emph{feasible} 
if 
$\gencond$ is 
feasible.
%
Otherwise, it is \emph{infeasible}.
\end{definition}
%
The following result is immediate from Definitions \ref{DefJoinabilityOfConditionalPairs} and \ref{DefFeasibleConditionalPair}.
%
\begin{proposition}\label{PropJoinabilityOfInfeasiblePairs}
Let $\cR$ be an \egtrs{} and $\genrelation,\genrelationbis$ be relations on terms.
Trivial and 
infeasible condition\-al pairs are 
$\joinOf{\genrelation}{\genrelationbis}$-joinable.
\end{proposition}
%
\subsection{Conditional critical and variable pairs}

Following \cite[Definition 59]{Lucas_LocalConferenceOfConditionalAndGeneralizedTermRewritingSystems_JLAMP24}, 
we describe two families of conditional pairs we use to prove and disprove $E$-confluence of \gtrs{s} $\cR=(\Symbols,\SPredicates,\mu,E,H,R)$:
\begin{itemize}
\item \emph{Conditional critical pairs (CCPs)} $\pi_{\alpha,p,\alpha'}$  of the form
\begin{eqnarray}
\langle\theta(s)[\theta(v)]_p,\theta(t)\rangle\IF\theta(\gencond),\sigma(\gencondbis)\label{LblGenericConditionalCriticalPair}
\end{eqnarray}
%
for variable disjoint rules $\alpha:s\to t\IF\gencond$ and $\alpha':u\to v\IF\gencondbis$ (rename if necessary)
and
an active non-variable position of $s$, $p\in\Pos^\mu_\Symbols(s)$ such that $s|_p$ and $u$ unify with \emph{mgu} $\theta$.
%
%
\begin{definition}[Proper, improper, and root 
CCPs]
\label{DefProperAndImproperCCPs}
If $\alpha$ and $\alpha'$ in a CCP $\ccpOf{\alpha,p,\alpha'}$ 
are renamed versions of \emph{the same} rule and $p=\toppos$, then $\ccpOf{\alpha,p,\alpha'}$ is called \emph{improper} (iCCP, simply written $\iccpOf{\alpha}$); otherwise, it is \emph{proper} (pCCP).\footnote{This terminology is borrowed from \cite[Definition 4.2]{AveLor_ConditionalRewriteSystemsWithExtraVariablesAndDeterministicLogicPrograms_LPAR94}.}
%
Furthermore, CCPs $\ccpOf{\alpha,\toppos,\alpha'}$ are called \emph{root} CCPs (rCCPs).\footnote{We borrow this terminology from \cite[Exercise 6.19]{BaaNip_TermRewritingAndAllThat_1998}.}
\end{definition}
%
Note that improper CCPs are root CCPs.

\begin{remark}[CCPs involving rules in $\eqoriented{E}$]
In our setting, rules of the form $\beta:x\rew{}\erhsr\IF\egencond$ for some term $\erhsr$ may belong to $\eqoriented{E}$ if an equation $x=\erhsr\IF\egencond$ (or $\erhsr=x\IF\egencond$) is in $E$.
%
They produce no CCP $\ccpOf{\beta,p,\alpha}$ for any position $p$ because the only possibility $p=\toppos$ is \emph{not} a non-variable position.
%
However, CCPs $\pi_{\alpha,p,\beta}$ for some rule $\alpha:\lhsr\to\rhsr\IF\gencond$ are possible.
%
Actually, since $\Var(\beta)\cap\Var(\alpha)=\emptyset$, $p$ could be any active, non-variable position of $\lhsr$,
see also \cite[footnote 1 in page 1166]{JouKir_CompletionOfASetOfRulesModuloASetOfEquations_SIAMJC86}, where such pairs are called \emph{variable critical pairs}.
\end{remark}
\item 
\emph{Conditional $\gbop$-variable pairs (CVPs)} $\cvpOf{\gbop}{\alpha,x,p}$ of the form
\begin{eqnarray}
\cvpOf{\gbop}{\alpha,x,p}:\langle s[x']_p,t\rangle\IF x\mathrel{\gbop} x', \gencond\label{LblGenericConditionalVariablePair}
\end{eqnarray}
which in this paper are \emph{parametric} on  
$\gbop$, a binary relation on terms,
$\alpha:s\to t\IF\gencond$ is a rule (where $s$ can be a variable), 
$x\in\Var^\mu(s)$ is an active variable of $s$,
$p\in\Pos^\mu_x(s)$ is an active position of $x$ in $s$, 
and $x'$ is a fresh variable.
%
We often talk about conditional variable pairs rather than 
conditional $\gbop$-variable pairs if no confusion arises.
%
In the following, $\CVP(U,\gbop)$ is the set of all $\gbop$-parametric 
CVPs (\ref{LblGenericConditionalVariablePair}) 
for a set of rules $U$.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Equational CCPs and Logic-based conditional critical pairs.}
\label{SecECCPsAndLCTRS}
%
Dealing with Peterson \& Stickel's rewriting, each reduction step $s\rew{\cR^\RMabbr,E}t$ involves the computation of $E$-matching substitutions $\sigma$ such that $s|_p\equequ{E}\sigma(\lhsr)$ for some rule $\lhsr\to\rhsr\IF\gencond$ and $t=s[\sigma(\rhsr)]_p$.
%
Accordingly, dealing with peaks involving at least one of such reduction steps (e.g., PS-r-peaks (\ref{LblAbstractRPeakJK86}) or 
PS-c-peaks  (\ref{LblAbstractCPeakJK86}))
may involve the use of \emph{$E$-unifiers} in the computation of 
critical pairs by replacing syntactic unifiers by $E$-unifiers $\theta$
leading to the notion of \emph{$E$-critical pairs} for \etrs{s}, see 
\cite[Definition 12]{JouKir_CompletionOfASetOfRulesModuloASetOfEquations_SIAMJC86}.
%
This notion has been extended to 
\emph{Generalized Rewrite Theories} 
\cite{BruMes_SemanticFoundationsForGeneralizedRewriteTheories_TCS06} as follows
\cite[Definition 6]{DurMes_OnTheChurchRosserAndCoherencePropertiesOfConditionalOrderSortedRewriteTheories_JLAP12}, which we slightly adapt to our setting.
%
Given terms $s$ and $t$, $\fS{CSU}_E(s,t)$ denotes a \emph{complete} (possibly infinite) set of $E$-unifiers of $s$ and $t$, i.e., for each $E$-unifier $\sigma$ of $s$ and $t$, there is 
$\theta\in\fS{CSU}_E(s,t)$ such that $\theta(s)\equequ{E}\theta(t)$ 
and there is a substitution $\tau$ such that 
for all $x\in\Variables$, 
$\sigma(x)\equequ{E}\tau(\theta(x))$
\cite[Definition 10.1.4]{BaaNip_TermRewritingAndAllThat_1998}.
%
\begin{itemize}
\item \emph{Conditional E-critical pairs (ECCPs)} $\eccpOf{\alpha,p,\alpha',\theta}$  of the form
\begin{eqnarray}
\langle\theta(s)[\theta(v)]_p,\theta(t)\rangle\IF\theta(\gencond),\sigma(\gencondbis)\label{LblGenericConditionalCriticalPair}
\end{eqnarray}
%
for variable disjoint  rules $\alpha:s\to t\IF\gencond$ and $\alpha:u\to v\IF\gencondbis$, an active non-variable position of $s$, $p\in\Pos^\mu_\Symbols(s)$, 
and $\theta\in\fS{CSU}_E(s|_p,u)$.
\end{itemize}
%
Of course, in order to obtain each $\theta$ above, an appropriate $E$-unification algorithm is ncessary. As mentioned in the introduction, however, that such an algorithm does not always exist.

In order to avoid the (computation of possibly infinitely many) $E$-unifiers of two terms with respect to a given set of equations $E$, we introduce the following.

\begin{definition}[Logic-based conditional critical pair]
%
Let $\alpha:s\to t\IF\gencond$ 
and
$\alpha':u\to v\IF\gencondbis$ be rules
sharing no variables, 
together with an active non-variable position $p\in\Pos^\mu_\Symbols(s)$.
%
The \emph{logic-based conditional critical pair} 
(LCCP for short) 
$\pi_{\alpha,p,\alpha'}$ of $\alpha$ at position $p$ with $\alpha'$ 
is:
\begin{eqnarray}
\lccpOf{\alpha,p,\alpha'}:\langle s[v]_p,t\rangle\IF s|_p\equequ{} u, \gencond,\gencondbis\label{LblLogicBaseDCP}
\end{eqnarray}
\end{definition}
%
Our terminology ``\emph{logic-based conditional critical pair}'' tries to avoid confusion with the \emph{$E$-critical pairs} for \etrs{s}
of 
\cite[Definition 12]{JouKir_CompletionOfASetOfRulesModuloASetOfEquations_SIAMJC86}
and also 
the
\emph{conditional critical pairs} for rewrite theories
(the ECCPs above).
We avoid the \emph{explicit} use of $E$-unifiers
by including the \emph{atom} 
$\lhsr|_p=\lhsr'$ in the conditional part of (\ref{LblLogicBaseDCP}).
%
Given a replacement map $\mu$ and
sets of rules $U$ and $V$, 
we let
$\GLCCP(U,V)=\{\lccpOf{\alpha,p,\alpha'}\mid\alpha:\lhsr\to\rhsr\IF\gencond\in U,p\in\Pos^\mu_\Symbols(\lhsr),\alpha'\in V
\}$.
%
As for CCPs (Definition \ref{DefProperAndImproperCCPs}), we distinguish between proper and improper LCCPs in the same way.

\section{Analysis of $\cR^\RMabbr$-reduction and coherence peaks}
\label{SecAnalysisOfRandCpeaks}

\subsection{$\cR^\RMabbr$-reduction peaks}

Given an \egtrs{} $\cR=(\Symbols,\SPredicates,\mu,E,H,R)$ and \emph{terms} $s$, $t$, and $t'$, we consider
\emph{r-peaks} (\ref{LblAbstractRPeak}) as follows:
%
\begin{eqnarray}
t\leftarrowWith{\cR^\RMabbr} s\rew{\cR^\RMabbr} t'\label{LblRMRPeakTerms}
\end{eqnarray}
%
Although a these peaks were considered
in \cite[Section 4]{Lucas_LocalConferenceOfConditionalAndGeneralizedTermRewritingSystems_JLAMP24}  for the analysis of local confluence of \ctrs{s} (and \gtrs{s}), we briefly reproduce it here as it is the basis of the analysis of $\cR^\RMabbr$-coherence peaks in Section \ref{SecCPeaks} and also of 
$\cR^\RMabbr,E$-peaks in Section \ref{SecAnalysisOfPSRandCpeaks}.

By Proposition \ref{PropUseOfRulesAndPositionsInRewritingSteps_EGTRSs}(\ref{PropUseOfRulesAndPositionsInRewritingSteps_EGTRSs_R}), 
there are positions $\ol{p},\ol{p'}\in\Pos^\mu(s)$,
%
rules $\alpha:\lhsr\to\rhsr\IF\gencond,\alpha':\lhsr'\to\rhsr'\IF\gencond'\in R^\RMabbr$
sharing no variable (rename if necessary), 
and a
substitution $\sigma$,
such that 
(i) $s|_{\ol{p}}=\sigma(\lhsr)$ and $\sigma(\gencond)$ hold; 
and 
(ii) $s|_{\ol{p'}}=\sigma(\lhsr')$ and $\sigma(\gencond')$ hold, i.e.,
every r-peak is of the form
\begin{eqnarray}
t = s[\sigma(\rhsr)]_{\ol{p}}~ \leftarrowWith{\cR^\RMabbr} ~ s[\underleftarrow{\sigma(\lhsr)}]_{\ol{p}}~~=& s & =~~s[\underrightarrow{\sigma(\lhsr')}]_{\ol{p'}} ~\rew{\cR^\RMabbr}~ s[\sigma(\rhsr')]_{\ol{p'}}=t'\label{GenericRMRPeakTerms}
\end{eqnarray}
%
%
Note from Table \ref{TableJoinabilityOfRpeaks}, that r-peaks are required to be $\ejoinability{\cR}$-joinable.

\subsubsection{Classes of r-peaks}

Depending on the relative location of $\ol{p}$ and $\ol{p'}$, %of 
different classes of r-peaks (\ref{GenericRMRPeakTerms}) are
distinguished. 

\medskip
\noindent
\textbf{\emph{Disjoint} r-peaks.}\label{SecDisjointEPeaks}
%
If $\ol{p}$ and $\ol{p'}$ in (\ref{GenericRMRPeakTerms})
are \emph{disjoint}, i.e., $\ol{p}\parallel \ol{p'}$, 
then $s=s[\sigma(\lhsr)]_{\ol{p}}[\sigma'(\lhsr')]_{\ol{p'}}=s[\sigma'(\lhsr')]_{\ol{p'}}[w]_{\ol{p}}$. 
Accordingly, (\ref{GenericRMRPeakTerms}) can be written as follows:
\begin{eqnarray}
t = s[\sigma(\rhsr)]_{\ol{p}} [\sigma(\lhsr')]_{\ol{p'}} \leftarrowWith{\cR^\RMabbr}    & 
s[\underleftarrow{\sigma(\lhsr)}]_{\ol{p}}[\underrightarrow{\sigma(\lhsr')}]_{\ol{p'}} 
& 
\rew{\cR^\RMabbr} 
s[\sigma(\lhsr)]_{\ol{p}}[\sigma(\rhsr')]_{\ol{p'}}  = t'
~~~\label{DisjointRPeakTerms}
\end{eqnarray}
Now, 
$
t = s[\sigma(\rhsr)]_{\ol{p}} [\underrightarrow{\sigma(\lhsr')}]_{\ol{p'}} ~\rew{\cR^\RMabbr}~ 
s[\sigma(\rhsr)]_{\ol{p}} [\sigma(\rhsr')]_{\ol{p'}} 
~\leftarrowWith{\cR^\RMabbr}~ s[\underleftarrow{\sigma(\lhsr)}]_{\ol{p}}[\sigma(\rhsr')]_{\ol{p'}}  = t'
$,
%
i.e., $t$ and $t'$ are 
$\joinability{\cR}$-joinable.

\medskip
\noindent
\textbf{\emph{Nested} r-peaks.}
%
If $\ol{p'}=\ol{p}.p\in\Pos^\mu(s)$ for 
some position $p$, then (\ref{GenericRMRPeakTerms})
can be written in one of the following possibilities, according to 
the position 
where the $\rew{\cR^\RMabbr}$-step applies
 (by abuse, we also use $t$ and $t'$).
 Without loss of generality, we can assume that the rightmost 
 $\rew{\cR^\RMabbr}$-step occurs \emph{below or on} the leftmost $\rew{\cR^\RMabbr}$-step and
we have
\begin{eqnarray}
t = \sigma(\lhsr)[\sigma(\rhsr')]_p ~\leftarrowWith{\cR^\RMabbr}   & \underrightarrow{\sigma(\lhsr)[\overleftarrow{\sigma(\lhsr')}]_p} & \rew{\cR^\RMabbr}~\sigma(\rhsr)=t'\label{NestedRMRPeakTermsRup}
\end{eqnarray}
%
where 
$p\geq\toppos$.
%
We distinguish two cases:
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $p\in\Pos^\mu_\Symbols(\lhsr)$, then $\sigma(\lhsr)|_p=\sigma(\lhsr'|_p)=\sigma(\lhsr')$, i.e.,
$\lhsr|_p$ and $\lhsr'$ unify and we say that
(\ref{NestedRMRPeakTermsRup}) is a \emph{critical r-peak} (Figure \ref{FigCriticalRPeakAndCCP}); 
\item If $p\notin\Pos^\mu_\Symbols(\lhsr)$, there is $x\in\Var^\mu(\lhsr)$ and $q\in\Pos^\mu_x(\lhsr)$ 
such that $\lhsr|_q=x$ and $q\leq p$; then we call
(\ref{NestedRMRPeakTermsRup}) a \emph{variable r-peak} (Figure \ref{FigVPeakAndCVP}).
\end{enumerate}
%
\begin{figure}[t]
\begin{tikzpicture}[node distance = 6cm, auto,scale=1,every node/.style={scale=1}]

\begin{definition}[$\mu$-homogeneous term; left $\mu$-homogeneous rule]
Given a replacement map $\mu$, we say that a term $t$ is 
\emph{$\mu$-homogeneous} if no variable occurs 
both active and frozen in $t$, i.e., $\Var^\mu(t)\cap\NVar{\mu}(t)=\emptyset$.
%
A rule $\lhsr\to\rhsr\IF\gencond$ is \emph{left-$\mu$-homogeneous} if $\lhsr$ is $\mu$-homogeneous.
\end{definition}
%
If the replacement map in use is $\muTop$ (all argument of all function symbols can be rewritten), then every term is $\muTop$-homogeneous.
%
\begin{definition}[$\mu$-compatible rule]
\label{DefMuCompatibleRule}
A rule $\lhsr\to\rhsr\IF\gencond$ is \emph{$\mu$-compatible} if 
(i) 
no active variable in $\lhsr$ is frozen in $\rhsr$, i.e., $\Var^\mu(\lhsr)\cap\NVar{\mu}(\rhsr)=\emptyset$, and
(ii) 
no active variable in $\lhsr$ occurs in $\gencond$, i.e., $\Var^\mu(\lhsr)\not\subseteq\Var(\gencond)$.
\end{definition}
%
If the replacement map in use is $\muTop$, then (i) in Definition 
\ref{DefMuCompatibleRule} trivially holds, as $\NVar{\mu}(t)=\emptyset$ for all terms $t$.

\begin{example}
\label{ExSumListsA_MuHomogeneousAndCompatible}
All rules in $R\:\cup\eqoriented{E}$ in Example \ref{ExSumListsA} are left-$\mu$-homogeneous (and also for $R^\showRMabbr$ in Example \ref{ExSumListsA_RM}).
%
All rules in $\eqoriented{E}$ are $\mu$-compatible.
%
Rules (\ref{ExSumListsA_rule1}) and (\ref{ExSumListsA_rule2}) in Example \ref{ExSumListsA} are $\mu$-compatible.
%
However, rules (\ref{ExSumListsA_rule3}) and (\ref{ExSumListsA_rule4}) are \emph{not} because all active variables in the left-hand sides of rules 
(i.e., $n$ in (\ref{ExSumListsA_rule3}) and 
$m$ in (\ref{ExSumListsA_rule3}))
occur in the conditional part.
\end{example}
%
We have the following.

\begin{proposition}[Joinable variable r-peaks]
\label{PropJoinableVariablePeaksForCriticalVariablesNotInCondition}
A variable r-peak (\ref{NestedRMRPeakTermsRup}) is 
$\lsjoinability{\cR^\RMabbr}$-joinable 
if 
$\alpha:\lhsr\to\rhsr\IF\gencond$ is left $\mu$-homogeneous and $\mu$-compatible.
%
Furthermore, if $x\in\Var^\mu(\rhsr)$, then (\ref{NestedRMRPeakTermsRup}) is 
$\sjoinability{\cR^\RMabbr}$-joinable.
\end{proposition}
%
\begin{proof}
Since $p\in\Pos^\mu(\sigma(\lhsr))-\Pos^\mu_\Symbols(\lhsr)$, we have 
$\lhsr|_q=x$ for some $x\in\Var^\mu(\lhsr)$ and $q\in\Pos^\mu_x(\lhsr)$
such that 
$p=q.u$ for some position $u$.
%
Note that $\sigma(x)=\sigma(x)[\sigma(\lhsr')]_u\rewAtPos{u}{\alpha'}\sigma(x)[\sigma(\rhsr')]_u$.
%
Let $Q=\{q_1,\ldots,q_n\}$ be the set of positions of occurrences of $x$ in $\lhsr$
(i.e., $q\in Q$).
%
Since $\lhsr$ is $\mu$-homogeneous, $Q\subseteq\Pos^\mu(\lhsr)$.
%
Thus, $\sigma(\lhsr)=\sigma(\lhsr)[\sigma(x)]_Q$
and we have $t = \sigma(\lhsr)[\sigma(\rhsr')]_p\rews{\alpha'}\sigma'(\lhsr)$, where
$\sigma'(x)=\sigma(x)[\sigma(\rhsr')]_u$ and $\sigma'(y)=\sigma(y)$ for all $y\neq x$.
%
By $\mu$-compatibility, 
$x$ does not occur in the conditional part $\gencond$ of $\alpha$.
Since $\sigma(\gencond)$ holds, we have that $\sigma'(\gencond)$ holds as well.
Thus,
 we have
$\sigma'(\lhsr)\rewAtPos{\toppos}{\alpha}\sigma'(\rhsr)$, i.e.,
$t\rews{\cR^\RMabbr}\sigma'(\rhsr)$.
%
We also have $t'=\sigma(\rhsr)\rews{\alpha'}\sigma'(\rhsr)$ by just reducing any possible occurrence of $\sigma(x)$ in $t'$, i.e., $\sigma(\rhsr)$, using $\alpha'$ (which is possible by $\mu$-compatibility). 
Hence, $t\rews{\alpha'}\sigma'(\lhsr)\rew{\alpha}\sigma'(\rhsr)\leftrews{\alpha'}\sigma(\rhsr)=t'$ proves $\lsjoinability{\cR^\RMabbr}$-joinability of (\ref{NestedRMRPeakTermsRup}).
%
Furthermore,  if $x\in\Var^\mu(\rhsr)$, then 
 $t'=\sigma(\rhsr)\rewp{\alpha'}\sigma'(\rhsr)$ proves $\sjoinability{\cR^\RMabbr}$-joinability of (\ref{NestedRMRPeakTermsRup}).
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Conditional pairs for nested r-peaks}
\label{SecConditionalPairsForNestedRpeaks}

Nested r-peaks (\ref{NestedRMRPeakTermsRup}) are captured by means of CCPs and
CVPs:
%
\begin{enumerate}
\item Critical r-peaks 
are captured by means of CCPs $\ccpOf{\alpha,p,\alpha'}$ for 
$\alpha:\lhsr\to\rhsr\IF\gencond,\alpha':\lhsr'\to\rhsr'\IF\gencond'\in R^\showRMabbr$ and $p\in\Pos^\mu_\Symbols(\lhsr)$ (Figure \ref{FigCriticalRPeakAndCCP}).
%
The set of \emph{feasible} CCPs obtained in this way is denoted $\CCP(\cR)$.
%
\item Variable r-peaks are captured by means of CVPs $\cvpROf{\alpha,x,p}$ for 
$\alpha:\lhsr\to\rhsr\IF\gencond\in R^\showRMabbr$,
$x\in\Var^\mu(\lhsr)$, and $p\in\Pos^\mu_x(\lhsr)$ (Figure \ref{FigVPeakAndCVP}).
%
The set of  
\emph{feasible} CVPs obtained in this way is denoted $\CVPofR(\cR)$.
\end{enumerate}
%
$\CCP(\cR)$ can be partitioned as $\CCP(\cR)=\pCCP(\cR)\uplus\iCCP(\cR)$, where $\pCCP(\cR)$ (resp.\ $\iCCP(\cR)$) consists of all feasible 
\emph{proper} (resp.\ \emph{improper}) CCPs.

\begin{proposition}
\label{PropJoinabilityOfImproperCriticalPeakssIn2CTRSs}
Improper CCPs $\iccpOf{\alpha}$ of 2-rules $\alpha$ 
are trivial. 
\end{proposition}
%
\begin{proof}
If $\alpha:\lhsr\to\rhsr\IF\gencond$ is a 2-rule, then $\Var(\rhsr)\subseteq\Var(\lhsr)$, and the renamed versions $\lhsr$ and $\lhsr'$ (with each variable $x$ in $\lhsr$ renamed as $x'$ in $\lhsr'$) of the left-hand side of $\alpha$ 
 unify with \emph{mgu} $\theta(x)=x'$ for all $x\in\Var(\lhsr)$. Thus, we also have 
 $\theta(\rhsr)=\theta(\rhsr')$.
 %
 Hence $\iccpOf{\alpha}:\langle\theta(\rhsr'),\theta(\rhsr)\rangle\IF\sigma(\gencond),\theta(\gencond')$ is trivial. 
\end{proof}
%
In contrast, dealing with 
rules $\alpha$ where
$\Var(\rhsr)\not\subseteq\Var(\lhsr)$, Proposition \ref{PropJoinabilityOfImproperCriticalPeakssIn2CTRSs} 
may \emph{fail} to hold (see
\cite[Example 4.1(a)]{AveLor_ConditionalRewriteSystemsWithExtraVariablesAndDeterministicLogicPrograms_LPAR94} for an example in the realm of \ctrs{s}).
%
\begin{remark}[Refining $\CCP(\cR)$]
\label{RemRefiningCCPR}
For the purposes of this paper, we only consider \emph{one} among all pairwise \emph{symmetric} CCPs in $\cR$.
% 
This is because the joinability notions we use with CCPs are \emph{symmetric}, i.e., the two compared terms can be switched without changing the joinability result.
%
In particular, we would choose one between the two root CCPs 
$\ccpOf{\alpha,\toppos,\alpha'}$ or $\ccpOf{\alpha',\toppos,\alpha}$ for rules $\alpha$ 
and $\alpha'$.
% 
Also, we can drop all iCCPs $\iccpOf{\alpha}$ of 2-rules $\alpha$ from $\CCP(\cR)$.
\end{remark}
%
\begin{example}
\label{ExSumListsA_CCP}
For $\cR$ in Example \ref{ExSumListsA}, using $R^\showRMabbr$
in Example \ref{ExSumListsA_RM}, 
there is a pCCP and an iCCP 
%
\begin{eqnarray}
\hspace{-0.5cm}\ccpOf{(\ref{ExSumListsA_rule3_RM}),\toppos,(\ref{ExSumListsA_rule4_RM})}: && 
\hspace{-0.5cm}\langle m+n,ms\rangle\IF 
\fS{Nat}(ms), ms\cto_\showRMabbr m \fS{\seqnat} \cfrozen{ns}, 
\fS{Nat}(m),  \fS{sum}(\cfrozen{ns})\cto_\showRMabbr n~~~\label{ExSumListsA_CCP_R_1}
\\
\iccpOf{(\ref{ExSumListsA_rule4_RM})}: &&
\hspace{-0.5cm}\langle m+n,m'+n'\rangle\IF 
ms\cto_\showRMabbr m \fS{\seqnat} \cfrozen{ns}, 
ms\cto_\showRMabbr m' \fS{\seqnat} \cfrozen{ns'}, 
\fS{Nat}(m),  \nonumber
\\
&& \hspace{2.85cm}\fS{Nat}(m'),\fS{sum}(\cfrozen{ns})\cto_\showRMabbr n,
\fS{sum}(\cfrozen{ns'})\cto_\showRMabbr n'~~\label{ExSumListsA_CCP_R_2}
\end{eqnarray}
%
Note that (\ref{ExSumListsA_CCP_R_1}) 
is \emph{infeasible}: assume that a substitution 
$\sigma$ satisfies the conditional part of 
(\ref{ExSumListsA_CCP_R_1}):
%
if $\fS{Nat}(\sigma(ms))$ holds, 
then $\sigma(ms)$ is of the form $\fS{s}^p(\fS{0})$ for some $p\geq 0$;
then, $\sigma(ms)$ is \emph{not} 
$\rews{\cR^\RMabbr/E}$-reducible to

%
Thus, $\CCP(\cR)=\{(\ref{ExSumListsA_CCP_R_2})\}$.
%
However, (\ref{ExSumListsA_CCP_R_2}) is $\ejoinability{\cR^\RMabbr}$-joinable.
This can be proved by induction on the structure of $\sigma(ms)$ for all
all substitutions $\sigma$ satisfying the conditional part of (\ref{ExSumListsA_CCP_R_2}).
\end{example}

\begin{proposition}
\label{PropEGTRSsAndPropertyAlpha}
Let $\cR=(\Symbols,\SPredicates,\mu,E,H,R)$ be an \egtrs{}.
%
Then, $\cR$ has property $\alpha$ iff 
all conditional pairs in $\CCP(\cR)\cup\CVPofR(\cR)$ are $\ejoinability{\cR}$-joinable. 
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
It follows by the thorough consideration in this section of
disjoint r-peaks 
(which are always $\joinability{\cR}$-joinable, hence $\ejoinability{\cR}$-joinable; 
and then (critical and variable) nested
r-peaks with associated conditional pairs mimicking their structure by the application of substitutions: CCPs for critical r-peaks and CVPs for variable r-peaks.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Joinability of CVPs}

\end{corollary}

\subsection{$\cR^\RMabbr$-coherence peaks}
\label{SecCPeaks}

Given an \egtrs{} $\cR=(\Symbols,\SPredicates,\mu,E,H,R)$ and terms $s$, $t$, $t'$, c-peaks (\ref{LblAbstractEPeak}) 
are of the form
%
\begin{eqnarray}
t\leftarrowWith{\cR^\RMabbr} s\rew{\eqoriented{E}} t'
\label{LblECohPeakTerms_Huet}
\end{eqnarray}
%
Given a term $s$,
%
positions $\ol{p},\ol{p'}\in\Pos^\mu(s)$,
%
a rule $\alpha:\lhsr\to\rhsr\IF\gencond\in R^\RMabbr$,
an \emph{oriented} equation 
$\beta:\elhsr\to\erhsr\IF\gencondbis\in\:\eqoriented{E}$
(sharing no variables with $\alpha$), 
and
substitution $\sigma$,
such that 
(i) $s|_{\ol{p}}=\sigma(\lhsr)$ and $\sigma(\gencond)$ holds; 
and 
(ii) $s|_{\ol{p'}}=\sigma(\elhsr)$ and $\sigma(\gencondbis)$ holds,
every c-peak (\ref{LblECohPeakTerms_Huet}) is of the form
%
\begin{eqnarray}
t = s[\sigma(\rhsr)]_{\ol{p}}~ \leftarrowWith{\cR^\RMabbr} ~ s[\underleftarrow{\sigma(\lhsr)}]_{\ol{p}}~~=& s & =~~s[\underrightarrow{\sigma(\elhsr)}]_{\ol{p'}} ~\rew{\eqoriented{E}}~
s[\sigma(\erhsr)]_{\ol{p'}}=t'\label{GenericECohPeakRewriting_Huet}
\end{eqnarray}
%
%
Note from Table \ref{TableJoinabilityOfRpeaks}, that c-peaks are required to be $\ejoinability{\cR}$-joinable.

\subsubsection{Classes of c-peaks}
%
In the following, we enumerate different classes of c-peaks according to the structure of involved terms and rules.

\medskip
\noindent
\textbf{\emph{Disjoint} c-peaks.} If $\ol{p}$ and $\ol{p'}$ in (\ref{GenericECohPeakRewriting_Huet})
are \emph{disjoint}, 
then $s=s[\sigma(\lhsr)]_{\ol{p}}[\sigma(\elhsr)]_{\ol{p'}}=s[\sigma(\elhsr)]_{\ol{p'}}[\sigma(\lhsr)]_{\ol{p}}$ and
we have:
\[
t = s[\sigma(\rhsr)]_{\ol{p}}[\sigma(\elhsr)]_{\ol{p'}}~\rew{\eqoriented{E}}~ 
%
s[\sigma(\rhsr)]_{\ol{p}} [\sigma(\erhsr)]_{\ol{p'}} 
%
\leftarrowWith{\cR^\RMabbr}~ s[\sigma(\lhsr)]_{\ol{p}}[\sigma(\erhsr)]_{\ol{p'}}  = t'
\]
Since $t ~\rew{\eqoriented{E}}~ 
s[\sigma(\rhsr)]_{\ol{p}} [\sigma(\erhsr)]_{\ol{p'}}$ implies $t ~\equequ{E}~ 
s[\sigma(\rhsr)]_{\ol{p}} [\sigma(\erhsr)]_{\ol{p'}}$,
we conclude 
$\rsejoinability{\cR^\RMabbr}$-joinability  of $t$ and $t'$.

\medskip
\noindent
\textbf{\emph{Nested} c-peaks.} If $\ol{p}$ and $\ol{p'}$ in (\ref{GenericECohPeakRewriting_Huet})
are \emph{not} disjoint,  then (\ref{GenericECohPeakRewriting_Huet})
can be written in one of the following two ways (again, by abuse, we use $t$ and $t'$; and $p\geq\toppos$):
%
\begin{eqnarray}
t = \sigma(\elhsr)[\sigma(\rhsr)]_p ~ \leftarrowWith{\cR^\RMabbr} & \underrightarrow{\sigma(\elhsr)[\overleftarrow{\sigma(\lhsr)}]_p} & \rew{\eqoriented{E}}  ~\sigma(\erhsr)=t'\label{NestedECohPeakRewritingEup_Huet}\\
%
t =  ~\sigma(\rhsr)\leftarrowWith{\cR^\RMabbr} & \overleftarrow{\sigma(\lhsr)[\underrightarrow{\sigma(\elhsr)}]_p} & \rew{\eqoriented{E}}  \sigma(\lhsr)[\sigma(\erhsr)]_p =t'\label{NestedECohPeakRewritingEdown_Huet}
\end{eqnarray}
%
Depending on the 
application (\emph{above} or \emph{below}) 
of the $\rew{\eqoriented{E}}$-step with respect 
to the application of the $\rew{\cR^\RMabbr}$-step, we call them
%
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{c-up-peaks} (\ref{NestedECohPeakRewritingEup_Huet}), where  
$\beta\in\eqoriented{E}$ is applied \emph{above} the application of $\alpha\in R^\RMabbr$.
We distinguish two cases:
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $p\in\Pos^\mu_\Symbols(\elhsr)$, then $\sigma(\elhsr)|_p=\sigma(\elhsr|_p)=\sigma(\lhsr)$, i.e.,
$\elhsr|_p$ and $\lhsr$ unify and we say that
(\ref{NestedECohPeakRewritingEup_Huet}) is a \emph{critical c-up-peak}; 
\item If $p\notin\Pos^\mu_\Symbols(\elhsr)$, then there is $x\in\Var^\mu(\elhsr)$ and $q\in\Pos^\mu_x(\elhsr)$ 
such that $\elhsr|_q=x$, $q\leq p$ and $\sigma(x)\rew{\cR^\RMabbr}\sigma(x')$ for some fresh variable $x'$. We say that
(\ref{NestedECohPeakRewritingEup_Huet}) is a \emph{variable c-up-peak}.
%
The case $p=\toppos$ and $\elhsr\in\Variables$, which is possible for rules $\beta\in\eqoriented{E}$, is considered here.
\end{enumerate}
%
\item  \emph{c-down-peaks} (\ref{NestedECohPeakRewritingEdown_Huet}), where $p>\toppos$ (the case $p=\toppos$ being treated as an $E$-up c-peak), i.e.,
$\beta\in\eqoriented{E}$ is applied \emph{below} the application of $\alpha\in R^\RMabbr$.
We distinguish two cases:
%
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $p\in\Pos^\mu_\Symbols(\lhsr)-\{\toppos\}$, 
then $\sigma(\lhsr)|_p=\sigma(\lhsr|_p)=\sigma(\elhsr)$, i.e.,
$\lhsr|_p$ and $\elhsr$ unify and we say that
(\ref{NestedECohPeakRewritingEdown_Huet}) is a \emph{critical c-down-peak}; 
\item If $p\notin\Pos^\mu_\Symbols(\lhsr)$, then there is $x\in\Var^\mu(\lhsr)$ and $q\in\Pos^\mu_x(\lhsr)$ 
such that $\lhsr|_q=x$, $q\leq p$ and $\sigma(x)\rew{\eqoriented{E}}\sigma(x')$ for some fresh variable $x'$. We say that
(\ref{NestedECohPeakRewritingEdown_Huet}) is a \emph{variable c-down-peak}.
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
%
\begin{proposition}[Joinable variable c-up-peaks]
\label{PropJoinableVariableEupCPeaksForCriticalVariablesNotInCondition}
A variable c-up-peak (\ref{NestedECohPeakRewritingEup_Huet}) is $\ejoinability{\cR^\RMabbr}$-joinable if 
$\beta$ is left-$\mu$-homogeneous and $\mu$-compatible.
%%
Furthermore, 
\begin{enumerate}
\item if $x$ occurs more than once in $\elhsr$, then (\ref{NestedECohPeakRewritingEup_Huet}) is $\lsejoinability{\cR^\RMabbr}$-joinable.
\item
If $x\in\Var^\mu(\erhsr)$, then (\ref{NestedECohPeakRewritingEup_Huet}) is 
$\rsejoinability{\cR^\RMabbr}$-joinable.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}
%
\begin{proof}
Since $p\notin\Pos^\mu_\Symbols(\elhsr)$, there is $x\in\Var^\mu(\elhsr)$
and $q\in\Pos^\mu_x(\elhsr)$ such that $\elhsr|_q=x$ and
$p=q.u$ for some position $u$.
%
Note that $\sigma(x)=\sigma(x)[\sigma(\lhsr)]_u\rewAtPos{u}{\alpha}\sigma(x)[\sigma(\rhsr)]_u$.
%
Let $Q=\{q_1,\ldots,q_n\}$ be the set of positions of occurrences of $x$ in $\elhsr$
(i.e., $q\in Q$).
%
Since $\elhsr$ is $\mu$-homogeneous, $Q\subseteq\Pos^\mu_x(\elhsr)$.
%
Thus, $\sigma(\elhsr)=\sigma(\elhsr)[\sigma(x)]_Q$
and we have $t = \sigma(\elhsr)[\sigma(\rhsr)]_p\rews{\alpha}\sigma'(\elhsr)$, where
$\sigma'(x)=\sigma(x)[\sigma(\rhsr)]_u$ and $\sigma'(y)=\sigma(y)$ for all $y\neq x$.
%
By $\mu$-compatibility of $\beta$, 
$x$ does not occur in the conditional part $\egencond$ of $\beta$.
Thus, since $\sigma(\egencond)$ holds, we have that $\sigma'(\egencond)$ holds as well.
Therefore,
 we have
$\sigma'(\elhsr)\rewAtPos{\toppos}{\beta}\sigma'(\erhsr)$, i.e., since $\beta\in\eqoriented{E}$,
$t\rews{\cR^\RMabbr}\circ\rew{\eqoriented{E}}\sigma'(\erhsr)$.
%
We also have $t'=\sigma(\erhsr)\rews{\alpha}\sigma'(\erhsr)$ by just reducing any possible occurrence of $\sigma(x)$ in $t'$ using $\alpha$ (which is possible by $\mu$-compatibility of $\beta$), i.e.,
$t\rews{\alpha}\sigma'(\elhsr)\equequ{E}\sigma'(\erhsr)\leftrews{\alpha}t'$,
 thus proving $\ejoinability{\cR^\RMabbr}$-joinability of (\ref{NestedECohPeakRewritingEup_Huet}).

If $x$ occurs more than once in $\elhsr$, then $t\rewp{\alpha}\sigma'(\elhsr)\equequ{E}\sigma'(\erhsr)\leftrews{\alpha}t'$, thus proving $\lsejoinability{\cR^\RMabbr}$-joinability of (\ref{NestedECohPeakRewritingEup_Huet}).
%
If $x\in\Var(\erhsr)$, then $t'=\sigma(\erhsr)\rewp{\alpha}\sigma'(\erhsr)$, thus proving 
$\rsejoinability{\cR^\RMabbr}$-joinability 
of (\ref{NestedECohPeakRewritingEup_Huet}).
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[$\mu$-linear term; $\mu$-left-linear rule and \egtrs]
\label{DefMuLeftLinearRule}
%
A term 
is \emph{$\mu$-linear} 
if no active variable in 
occurs twice.
%
A rule $\lhsr\to\rhsr\IF\gencond$ is \emph{$\mu$-left-linear} if $\lhsr$ is $\mu$-linear.
%
An \egtrs{} $\cR=(\Symbols,\SPredicates,\mu,E,H,R)$ 
is $\mu$-left-linear if all rules in $R$ 
are.
\end{definition}
%
Linear terms are, of course, $\mu$-left-linear, but not vice versa.
%
For instance, $t=\fS{f}(x,x)$ is $\muBot$-left-linear, as no occurrence of $x$ is active in $t$ due to $\muBot(\fS{f})=\emptyset$.

\begin{proposition}[Joinable variable c-down-peaks]
\label{PropJoinableVariableEdownCPeaksForCriticalVariablesNotInCondition}
A variable c-down-peak (\ref{NestedECohPeakRewritingEdown_Huet}) is  $\rsejoinability{\cR^\RMabbr,E}$-joinable
if $\alpha$ is left-$\mu$-homogeneous
and
$\mu$-compatible.
%
Furthermore, if $\alpha$ is $\mu$-left-linear,
then (\ref{NestedECohPeakRewritingEdown_Huet}) is 
$\rsejoinability{\cR^\RMabbr}$-joinable.
\end{proposition}
%
\begin{proof}
Since $p\notin\Pos^\mu_\Symbols(\lhsr)$, there is 
$x\in\Var^\mu(\lhsr)$ and $q\in\Pos^\mu_x(\lhsr)$ such that 
$\lhsr|_q=x$ and
$p=q.u$ for some position $u$.
%
Note that $\sigma(x)=\sigma(x)[\sigma(\elhsr)]_u\rewAtPos{u}{\beta}\sigma(x)[\sigma(\erhsr)]_u$.
%
Let $U=\{u_1,\ldots,u_n\}$, for some $n\geq 0$, 
be the set of positions of occurrences of $x$ in $\rhsr$.
%
Thus, $t=\sigma(\rhsr)=\sigma(\rhsr)[\sigma(x)]_U$.
%
By $\mu$-compability, no occurrence of $x$ is frozen in $\rhsr$.
%
Thus, we have
$t\rews{\eqoriented{E}}\sigma'(\rhsr)$ for some substitution $\sigma'$ such that
$\sigma'(x)=\sigma(x)[\sigma(\erhsr)]_u$
and $\sigma'(y)=\sigma(y)$ if $y\neq x$, i.e., for each occurrence of $x$ in $\rhsr$,
$\sigma(x)$ is reduced using $\beta$, i.e., for all $z\in\Variables$,
$\sigma(z)\equequ{E}\sigma'(z)$.
%
Since $\lhsr$ is $\mu$-homogeneous all occurrences of $x$ in $\lhsr$ are active and we have
$t'=\sigma(\lhsr)[\sigma(\erhsr)]_p\rews{\eqoriented{E}}\sigma'(\lhsr)$, i.e.,
$t'\equequ{E}\sigma'(\lhsr)$.
%
By $\mu$-compability, $x$ does not occur in the conditional part $\gencond$ of $\alpha$.
Since $\sigma(\gencond)$ holds, 
we have that $\sigma'(\gencond)$ holds as well.
%
Thus, $t\equequ{E}\sigma'(\rhsr)\leftrew{\alpha}\sigma'(\lhsr)\equequ{E}t'$, i.e.,
$t\equequ{E}\sigma'(\rhsr)\leftrew{\cR^\RMabbr,E}t'$.
%
Hence, 
(\ref{NestedECohPeakRewritingEdown_Huet}) is $\rsejoinability{\cR^\RMabbr,E}$-joinable.

If $\lhsr$ is $\mu$-left-linear, then $q$ is the only position of $x$ in $\lhsr$
and 
$t\equequ{E}\sigma'(\rhsr)\leftrew{\alpha}\sigma'(\lhsr)=t'$,
thus proving 
$\rsejoinability{\cR^\RMabbr}$-joinability
of (\ref{NestedECohPeakRewritingEdown_Huet}).
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Conditional pairs for nested c-peaks}

Nested c-peaks are captured by means of 
CCPs and
CVPs as follows:
%
\begin{enumerate}
\item Regarding c-up-peaks (\ref{NestedECohPeakRewritingEup_Huet}),
\begin{enumerate}
\item Critical c-up-peaks 
are captured by means of CCPs $\pi_{\beta,p,\alpha}$ for 
$\beta:\elhsr\to\erhsr\IF\egencond\spcrel{\in}\eqoriented{E}$,
$\alpha:\lhsr\to\rhsr'\IF\gencond'\in R^\showRMabbr$, and $p\in\Pos^\mu_\Symbols(\elhsr)$.
%
The set of feasible CCPs of this form is $\CCP(E,\cR)$.
%
\item Variable c-up-peaks are captured by means of CVPs 
$\cvpROf{\beta,x,p}$
for 
$\beta:\elhsr\to\erhsr\IF\egencond\in\eqoriented{E}$,
$x\in\Var^\mu(\elhsr)$, and $p\in\Pos^\mu_x(\elhsr)$.
%
The set of feasible CVPs of this form is $\CVPofR(E)$.
\end{enumerate}

\item Regarding c-down-peaks (\ref{NestedECohPeakRewritingEdown_Huet}),
\begin{enumerate}
\item Critical c-down-peaks 
are captured by means of CCPs $\pi_{\alpha,p,\beta}$ for 
$\alpha:\lhsr\to\rhsr\IF\gencond\in R^\showRMabbr$,
$\beta:\elhsr\to\erhsr\IF\egencond\in\eqoriented{E}$, and $p\in\Pos^\mu_\Symbols(\lhsr)-\{\toppos\}$.
%
The set of feasible CCPs of this form is $\CCP(\cR,E)$.
%
\item Variable c-down-peaks are captured by means of CVPs $\cvpEqOneOf{\alpha,x,p}$ for 
$\alpha:\lhsr\to\rhsr\IF\gencond\in R^\showRMabbr$,
$x\in\Var^\mu(\lhsr)$, and $p\in\Pos^\mu_x(\lhsr)$.
%
The set of feasible CVPs of this form is $\CVPofEqOne(\cR)$.
%
The intended meaning of $\equone{}$ in these CVPs 
is $\rew{\eqoriented{E}}$.
%
We use $\equone{}$ to improve readability.
\end{enumerate}
%
\end{enumerate}
%
According to Table \ref{TableJoinabilityOfRpeaks}, 
the joinability conditions for all these CCPs and CVPs 
to prove property $\gamma$ is $\ejoinability{\cR^\RMabbr}$.
%
\begin{proposition}
\label{PropEGTRSsAndPropertyGamma}
Let $\cR=(\Symbols,\SPredicates,\mu,E,H,R)$ be an \egtrs{}.
%
Then, $\cR$ has property $\gamma$ iff 
all conditional pairs in $\CCP(E,\cR)\cup\CCP(\cR,E)\cup\CVPofR(E)\cup\CVPofEqOne(\cR)$ are $\ejoinability{\cR}$-joinable. 
\end{proposition}


\begin{proof}
It follows by the thorough consideration in this section of
disjoint c-peaks 
(which are always $\ejoinability{\cR}$-joinable); 
and then (critical and variable) nested
c-up and c-down peaks with associated conditional pairs mimicking their structure by the application of substitutions: CCPs for critical c-up and c-down peaks and CVPs for variable c-up and c-down peaks.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Joinability of CVPs}

According to Propositions \ref{PropJoinableVariableEupCPeaksForCriticalVariablesNotInCondition}
and \ref{PropJoinableVariableEdownCPeaksForCriticalVariablesNotInCondition}, we have the following.

\begin{corollary}
\label{CoroJoinableVariablePairsForECoherencePeaks}
Let $\cR=(\Symbols,\SPredicates,\mu,E,H,R)$ be an \egtrs{}, 
$\alpha:\lhsr\to\rhsr\IF\gencond\in R^\RMabbr$ and $\beta:\elhsr\to\erhsr\IF\egencond\in\eqoriented{E}$.
Then, 
\begin{enumerate}
\item\label{CoroJoinableVariablePairsForECoherencePeaks_CVPto}
 $\pi^\to_{\beta,x,p}$ is $\ejoinability{\cR^\RMabbr}$-joinable if 
$\beta$ is left-$\mu$-homogeneous and $\mu$-compatible.
Furthermore, 
\begin{enumerate}
\item\label{CoroJoinableVariablePairsForECoherencePeaks_CVPto_XmoreThanOnce}
  If $x$ occurs more than once in $\elhsr$, then  $\pi^\to_{\beta,x,p}$ is $\lsejoinability{\cR^\RMabbr}$-joinable.
  %
\item\label{CoroJoinableVariablePairsForECoherencePeaks_CVPto_XinERHSR}
 If $x\in\Var(\erhsr)$, then $\pi^\to_{\beta,x,p}$ is $\rsejoinability{\cR^\RMabbr}$-joinable.
\end{enumerate}
%
\item\label{CoroJoinableVariablePairsForECoherencePeaks_CVPeq}
 $\cvpEqOneOf{\alpha,x,p}$ is $\lsejoinability{\cR,E}$-joinable if 
$\alpha$ is left-$\mu$-homogeneous and $\mu$-compatible.
%
Furthermore, 
if $\alpha$ is $\mu$-left-linear, then $\cvpEqOneOf{\alpha,x,p}$ is $\lsejoinability{\cR^\RMabbr}$-joinable.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}
%
\begin{remark}[From right- to left- strict joinability in CVPs]
\label{RemFromRightToLeftStrictJoinability}
Note that $\rsejoinability{\cR^\RMabbr,E}$- and $\rsejoinability{\cR^\RMabbr}$-joinability of variable c-down peaks (\ref{NestedECohPeakRewritingEdown_Huet}) in Proposition \ref{PropJoinableVariableEdownCPeaksForCriticalVariablesNotInCondition}
become
$\lsejoinability{\cR^\RMabbr,E}$- and $\lsejoinability{\cR^\RMabbr}$-joinability
of the corresponding CVPs in Corollary \ref{CoroJoinableVariablePairsForECoherencePeaks}(\ref{CoroJoinableVariablePairsForECoherencePeaks_CVPeq}).
%
The reason is that the usual structure of CVPs introduces an \emph{inversion} of the represented terms in c-down peaks (\ref{NestedECohPeakRewritingEdown_Huet}). Thus, in order to keep the appropriate joinability condition for the represented peaks, the obtained joinabilitty conditions for CVPs need to be consistently inverted.
%
Although this difference is not crucial in the current setting where only $\ejoinability{\cR^\RMabbr}$ is required for all peaks (see Table \ref{TableJoinabilityOfRpeaks}), it will be important in the following sections, where \emph{asymmetric} joinability conditions could be required for PS-c-peaks (Table \ref{TableJoinabilityOfRpeaksJK86}).
\end{remark}

\cvpEqOneOf{(\ref{ExHuet80_RemarkPage818variant_rule1}),x,2}:
&& \langle\fS{f}(x,x'),\fS{g}(x)\rangle \IF  x\equone{}x'\label{ExHuet80_RemarkPage818variant_ECVP2}
\\
\cvpEqOneOf{(\ref{ExHuet80_RemarkPage818variant_rule1b}),x,1}:
&& \langle\fS{f}(x',x),\fS{h}(x)\rangle \IF  x\equone{}x'\label{ExHuet80_RemarkPage818variant_ECVP3}
\\
\cvpEqOneOf{(\ref{ExHuet80_RemarkPage818variant_rule1b}),x,2}:
&& \langle\fS{f}(x,x'),\fS{h}(x)\rangle \IF  x\equone{}x'\label{ExHuet80_RemarkPage818variant_ECVP4}
\\
\cvpEqOneOf{(\ref{ExHuet80_RemarkPage818variant_rule4}),x,1}:
&& \langle\fS{g}(x'),x\rangle \IF  x\equone{}x'\label{ExHuet80_RemarkPage818variant_ECVP5}
\\
\cvpEqOneOf{(\ref{ExHuet80_RemarkPage818variant_rule5}),x,1}:
&& \langle\fS{h}(x'),x\rangle \IF  x\equone{}x'\label{ExHuet80_RemarkPage818variant_ECVP6}
\end{eqnarray}
%
Note that (\ref{ExHuet80_RemarkPage818variant_CCP_ER_1}) 
and (\ref{ExHuet80_RemarkPage818variant_CCP_ER_2}), from $\CCP(E,\cR)$, 
are 
$\rsjoinability{\cR^\RMabbr}$-joinable.
%
The CVPs (\ref{ExHuet80_RemarkPage818variant_ECVP1})--
(\ref{ExHuet80_RemarkPage818variant_ECVP4}), from $\CVPofEqOne(E)$, are
all $\lsjoinability{\cR^\RMabbr}$-joinable:
if $\sigma$ satisfies their common conditional part, 
$x\equone{}x'$ 
then $\sigma=\{ x\mapsto C[\fS{a}], x'\mapsto C[\fS{b}]\}$
or $\sigma=\{ x\mapsto C[\fS{b}], x'\mapsto C[\fS{a}]\}$
for some context $C[\:]$.
%
Then (in particular for (\ref{ExHuet80_RemarkPage818variant_ECVP1}); for the others it is similar), 
\[\begin{array}{rcl}
\sigma(\fS{f}(x',x)) & = & \fS{f}(C[\fS{b}],C[\fS{a}])\rewp{}\fS{f}(C[\fS{c}],C[\fS{c}])\rew{}\fS{g}(C[\fS{c}])
\\ 
\sigma(\fS{g}(x)) & = & \fS{g}(C[\fS{a}])\rew{}\fS{g}(C[\fS{c}])
\end{array}
\]
and similarly for the second possible $\sigma$, as required.
%
By Corollary \ref{CoroJoinableVariablePairsForECoherencePeaks}(\ref{CoroJoinableVariablePairsForECoherencePeaks_CVPeq}), 
the CVPs (\ref{ExHuet80_RemarkPage818variant_ECVP5}) and
(\ref{ExHuet80_RemarkPage818variant_ECVP6}) are
$\lsjoinability{\cR^\RMabbr}$-joinable, as rules 
(\ref{ExHuet80_RemarkPage818variant_rule4}) and
(\ref{ExHuet80_RemarkPage818variant_rule5}) are $\muTop$-left-linear (hence $\muTop$-homogeneous)
and $\muTop$-compatible.
\end{example}

\begin{theorem}
\label{TheoEConfluenceOfETerminatingEGTRSsHuet}
Let $\cR=(\Symbols,\SPredicates,\mu,E,H,R)$ be an \egtrs{}.
%
\begin{enumerate}
\item\label{TheoEConfluenceOfETerminatingEGTRSsHuet_EConfluence} 
If $\cR$ is $E$-terminating, then it is $E$-confluent if all pairs in 
\[\CCP(\cR)\cup\CVPofR(\cR)\cup\CCP(E,\cR)\cup\CCP(\cR,E)
\cup
\CVPofR(E)\cup\CVPofEqOne(\cR)
\]
are $\ejoinability{\cR}$-joinable.

\item\label{TheoEConfluenceOfETerminatingEGTRSsHuet_NonEConfluent} 
If there is a \emph{non}-$\cR/E$-joinable $\pi\in\CCP(\cR)\cup\CVPofR(\cR)$, then $\cR$ is not $E$-confluent.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}
%
\begin{proof}
\begin{enumerate}
\item By Propositions \ref{PropEGTRSsAndPropertyAlpha} and
\ref{PropEGTRSsAndPropertyGamma}, $\rew{\cR^\RMabbr}$ 
satisfies properties $\alpha$ and $\gamma$. 
%
By Corollary \ref{CoroEConfluence_Huet80}, $\cR$ is $E$-confluent.
\item Since conditional pairs in $\CCP(\cR)\cup\CVPofR(\cR)$ represent all $\peakOf{\cR^\RMabbr}{\cR^\RMabbr}$-peaks, the claim follows by Corollary \ref{CoroDisprovingEConcludenceByNonREJoinableLocalConfluencePeaks}.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}
%

\end{example}
